1
河東道，蓋古冀州之域，漢河東、太原、上黨、西河、鴈門、代郡及鉅鹿、常山、趙國、廣平國之地。 河中、絳、晉、慈、隰、石、太原、汾、忻、潞、澤、沁、遼為實沈分，代、雲、朔、蔚、武、新、嵐、憲為大梁分。 為府二，州十九，縣百一十。 其名山：雷首、介、霍、五臺。 其大川：汾、沁、丹、潞。 厥賦：布、襺。 厥貢：布、席、豹尾、熊鞹、鵰羽。 河中府河東郡，赤。 本蒲州，上輔。 義寧元年治桑泉，武德三年徙治河東。 開元八年置中都，為府； 是年罷都，復為州。 乾元三年復為府。 土貢：氈、𪌭扇、龍骨、棗、鳳棲梨。 戶七萬八百，口四十六萬九千二百一十三。 縣十三。 有府十八，曰興政、復化、寧靜、洞渦、五泉、昌寧、志節、汾陽、靜智、信童、晉原、聞陽、清定、豐川、竹馬、攘胡、西胡、文谷。城中有天兵軍，開元十一年廢。 有府三十三，曰興樂、德義、胡壁、龍亭、清源、永和、陶城、霍山、瀵水、首陽、壽貴、歸仁、長渠、虞城、通閏、寶鼎、鹽海、歸淳、大陽、永安、奉信、永興、右威、汾陰、甘泉、平川、安保、石門、綏化、壇道、安邑、崇義、六軍。又有耀德軍，乾元二年置，廣德二年廢。河東，次赤。有芳醞監、汲河以釀，武德三年置，貞觀十年廢。南有風陵關，聖曆元年置。有歷山。河西，次赤。開元八年析河東置，尋省。乾元三年更同州之朝邑曰河西，來屬。大曆五年復還同州，析朝邑、河東別置。有蒲津關，一名蒲坂。開元十二年鑄八牛，牛有一人策之，牛下有山，皆鐵也，夾岸以維浮梁。十五年自朝邑徙河瀆祠于此。臨晉，次畿。本桑泉，武德三年析置溫泉縣，九年省。天寶十三載更名。解，次畿。本虞鄉，武德元年更名。貞觀十七年省，以地入虞鄉，二十二年復置。有鹽池，又有女鹽池。有紫泉監，乾元元年置，有銅穴十二。猗氏，次畿，有孤山。虞鄉，次畿。武德元年別置。貞觀二十二年省，以地入解。天授二年復置。北十五里有涑水渠，貞觀十七年，刺史薛萬徹開，自聞喜引涑水下入臨晉。永樂，次畿。武德元年置，本隸芮州，州廢，隸鼎州，貞觀八年來屬，後又隸虢州，神龍元年復故。有雷首山。安邑，次畿。義寧元年以安邑、虞鄉、夏置安邑郡。武德元年曰虞州，又析置桐鄉縣。三年析安邑置興樂縣。貞觀元年省。十七年州廢，省桐鄉入聞喜，以安邑、解來屬。至德二載更安邑曰虞邑，乾元元年隸陝州，大曆四年復故名，元和三年來屬。有龍池宮，開元八年置。有鹽池，與解為兩池，大曆十二年生乳鹽，賜名寶應靈慶池。有銀監。寶鼎，次畿。本汾陰。義寧元年以汾陰、龍門置汾陰郡，武德元年曰泰州，州廢來屬。開元十年獲寶鼎，更名。有后土祠。襄陵，緊。本隸晉州，元和十四年隸絳州，大和元年來屬。稷山，上。 河東，河西，臨晉，解，猗氏，次畿，有孤山。 虞鄉，永樂，安邑，寶鼎，襄陵，稷山，上。 本隸絳州，唐末來屬。 有稷山。 萬泉，上。本隸泰州，武德三年析稷山、安邑、猗氏、汾陰、龍門置，州廢隸絳州，大順二年來屬。有介山。龍門。次畿。武德二年徙泰州來治，五年析置萬春縣。貞觀十七年州廢，省萬春入龍門，隸絳州。元和初來屬。有龍門關。有高祖廟，貞觀中置。北三十里有瓜谷山堰，貞觀十年築。東南二十三里有十石壚渠，二十三年，縣令長孫恕鑿，溉田良沃，畝收十石。西二十一里有馬鞌塢渠，亦恕所鑿。有龍門倉，開元二年置。晉州平陽郡，望。 萬泉，龍門。 晉州晉州平陽郡，望。 本臨汾郡，義寧二年更名。 土貢：蠟燭，有平陽院礬官。 戶六萬四千八百三十六，口四十二萬九千二百二十一。 縣八。 平棘，上。東二里有廣潤陂，引太白渠以注之，東南二十里有畢泓，皆永徽五年令弓志元開，以畜洩水利。寧晉，緊。本癭陶，天寶元年更名。地旱鹵。西南有新渠，上元中，令程處默引洨水入城以溉田，經十餘里，地用豐潤，民食乃甘。昭慶，望。本大陸，武德四年曰象城，天寶元年更名。西南二十里有建初陵、啟運陵，二陵共塋。城下有灃水渠，儀鳳三年，令李玄開，以溉田通漕。柏鄉，上。 龍岡，上。武德元年析龍岡、內丘置青山縣，開成五年省入焉。沙河，上。武德元年置溫州，四年州廢，來屬。有鐵。南和，緊。武德元年置和州，四年州廢，來屬。鉅鹿，上。武德元年置起州，幷析置白起縣。四年州廢，省白起，以鉅鹿隸趙州。貞觀元年來屬。有大陸澤。有鹹泉，煮而成鹽。平鄉，上。武德元年置封州，四年州廢，來屬。貞元中，刺史元誼徙漳水，自州東二十里出，至鉅鹿北十里入故河。任，中。武德四年置。堯山，上。本柏仁。武德元年置東龍州，四年州廢，隸趙州，五年來屬。天寶元年更名。內丘。上。武德四年隸趙州，五年來屬。有鐵。洺州廣平郡，望。 有府十五，曰神山、平陽、豐寧、冀城、安信、萬安、益昌、英臺、岳陽、仁壽、高陽、臨汾、晉安、白澗、高華、仁德。 臨汾，望。東北十里有高梁堰，武德中引高梁水溉田，入百金泊。貞觀十三年為水所壞。永徽二年，刺史李寬自東二十五里夏柴堰引潏水溉田，令陶善鼎復治百金泊，亦引潏水溉田。乾封二年堰壞，乃西引晉水。有姑射山。洪洞，望。本楊，義寧二年更名。武德元年析洪洞、臨汾置西河縣，貞觀十七年省入臨汾。神山，中。本浮山，武德二年析襄陵置。東南有羊角山。四年以老子祠更名。岳陽，中。 臨汾，洪洞，神山，岳陽，中。 東有府城關。 有鐵。 聞喜，望。武德元年置。有銅冶。東南三十五里有沙渠，儀鳳二年，詔引中條山水于南坡下，西流經十六里，溉涑陰田。垣。上。義寧元年以垣、王屋置邵原郡，又置清廉、亳城二縣。武德元年曰邵州。二年置長泉縣，是年，以長泉隸懷州，後省。五年省亳城入垣。貞觀元年州廢，省清廉入垣，來屬。龍朔二年隸洛州，長安二年復舊；貞元三年隸陝州，元和三年復舊。慈州文城郡，下。 霍邑，上。義寧元年以霍邑、趙城、汾西、靈石置霍山郡。武德元年曰呂州。貞觀十七年州廢，以靈石隸汾州，霍邑、趙城、汾西來屬。有西北鎮霍山祠。趙城，上。義寧元年析霍邑置。汾西，中。 霍邑，趙城，汾西，中。 有鐵。 冀氏。 中。 絳州絳郡，雄。 土貢：白縠、粱米、梨、墨、蠟燭、防風。 戶八萬二千二百四，口五十一萬七千三百三十一。 縣七。 西南有橫海軍，開元十四年置，天寶後廢，大曆元年復置。清池，緊。西北五十五里有永濟隄二，永徽二年築。西四十五里有明溝河隄二，西五十里有李彪淀東隄及徒駭河西隄，皆三年築。西四十里有衡漳隄二，顯慶元年築。西北六十里有衡漳東隄，開元十年築。東南二十里有渠，注毛氏河，東南七十里有渠，注漳，並引浮水，皆刺史姜師度開。西南五十七里有無棣河，東南十五里有陽通河，皆開元十六年開。南十五里有浮河隄、陽通河隄，又南三十里有永濟北隄，亦是年築。有甘井二，十年，令毛某母老，苦水鹹無以養，縣舍穿地，泉湧而甘，民謂之毛公井。有鹽。鹽山，緊。武德四年置東鹽州，五年，以景州之清池幷析鹽山置浮水縣以隸之。貞觀元年州廢，省浮水，以清池、鹽山來屬。有鹽。長蘆，上。本隸瀛州。武德四年，以長蘆、平舒、魯城及滄州之清池置景州。貞觀元年州廢，以平舒還隸瀛州，長蘆、魯城來屬。樂陵，上。本隸棣州，武德八年來屬，大和二年又隸棣州，尋復來屬。饒安，上。武德四年析置鬲津縣，貞觀元年省入樂陵。無棣，上。貞觀元年省入陽信，八年復置，大和二年隸棣州，尋來屬。有無棣溝通海，隋末廢，永徽元年，刺史薛大鼎開。乾符。上。本魯城，乾符元年生野稻水穀二千餘頃，燕、魏飢民就食之，因更名。景州，上。 陸澤，上。先天二年析饒陽、鹿城置。饒陽，望。武德四年析置無蔞縣，貞觀元年省。束鹿，上。本鹿城，天寶十五載更名。安平，上。博野，望。本隸滿州。武德五年以博野、清苑、定州之義豐置蠡州，八年州廢，縣還故屬，九年復以博野、清苑置。貞觀元年州廢，以博野、清苑隸瀛州。永泰中以博野來屬。元和十年復隸瀛州，後又來屬。樂壽，緊。本隸瀛州，大曆中來屬，元和十年復隸瀛州，後又來屬。下博。上。本隸冀州，貞觀元年來屬。州廢，還隸冀州。後又來屬。開元二年隸冀州。永泰元年復來屬。有永寧軍，貞元十年置。趙州趙郡，望。 有府三十三，曰新田、大平、正平、武城、長社、大鄉、垣城、涑川、絳川、蓋松、鳳亭、延光、平原、高涼、神泉、桐鄉，萬泉、翼城、皮氏、董澤、零原、石池、延福、永康、景山、周陽、夏臺、古亭、崇樂、絳邑、長平、武陽、蒲邑。 正平，望。 西有武平故關。 太平，緊。有太平關，貞觀七年置。曲沃，望。東北三十五里有新絳渠，永徽元年，令崔翳引古堆水溉田百餘頃。南十三里山有銅。翼城，望。義寧元年以翼城、絳置翼城郡，幷井置小鄉縣。武德元年曰澮州，二年曰北澮州，四年州廢，縣皆來屬，九年省小鄉入翼城。天祐二年更曰澮川。有銅源、翔臯錢坊二。有澮高山，有銅，有鐵。絳，望。 太平，曲沃，翼城，絳，望。 有鐵。 聞喜，垣。 慈州慈州文城郡，下。 本汾州，武德五年曰南汾州，貞觀八年更名。 土貢：白蜜、蠟燭。 戶萬一千六百一十六，口六萬二千四百八十六。 縣五。 河間，望。武德五年置武垣縣，貞觀元年省入焉。西北百里有長豐渠，二十一年，刺史朱潭開。又西南五里有長豐渠，開元二十五年，刺史盧暉自束城、平舒引滹沱東入淇通漕，溉田五百餘頃。高陽，上。武德四年以高陽、鄚、博野、清苑置滿州。五年以博野、清苑隸蠡州。貞觀元年州廢，以鄚、高陽來屬。平舒，上。 汲，緊。武德元年以汲、新鄉置義州。四年州廢，以汲來屬，新鄉隸殷州。衞，緊。貞觀十七年省清淇縣入焉。長安三年復置清淇縣。神龍元年又省。御水有石堰一，貞觀十七年築。有蘇門山。共城，上。武德元年以縣置共州，幷析置凡城縣。四年州廢，省凡城，以共城隸殷州。六年省博望縣入焉。有白鹿山。新鄉，望。 有河陽軍，建中四年置。河陽，望。武德四年，析懷州之河陽、集城、溫於河陽宮置盟州。八年州廢，省集城入河陽，溫隸懷州。顯慶二年隸洛州。有河陽關。有回洛故城。有池，永徽四年引濟水漲之，開元中以畜黃魚。汜水，望。本隸鄭州，武德四年析置成臯縣，貞觀元年省，顯慶二年隸洛州，垂拱四年曰廣武，神龍元年復故名。有虎牢關。東南有成臯故關。西南有旋門故關。有牛口渚。西一里伏龜山有昭武廟，會昌五年置。河陰，望。開元二十二年析汜水、滎澤、武陟置，隸河南府，領河陰倉，會昌三年來屬。有梁公堰，在河、汴間，開元二年，河南尹李傑因故渠濬之，以便漕運。溫，望。武德四年，隋令周仲隱以縣去王世充，來降，置平州，名縣城曰李城；是年州廢，隸懷州。顯慶二年隸洛州。濟源。望。武德二年，王世充將丁伯德以縣來降，置西濟州，又析置溴陽、蒸川、邵原三縣。四年州廢，省溴陽、蒸川、邵原，以濟源隸懷州。貞觀元年省懷州之軹縣入焉。顯慶二年隸洛州。有枋口堰，大和五年，節度使溫造浚古渠，溉濟源、河內、溫、武陟田五千頃。有濟瀆祠、北海祠。西有故軹關。懷州河內郡，雄。 有府三，曰五臺、東冶、鴈門。有守捉兵。其北有大同軍，本大武軍，調露二年曰神武軍，天授二年曰平狄軍，大足元年復更名。其西有天安軍，天寶十二載置。又有代北軍，永泰元年置。 有府三，曰仵城、吉昌、平昌。 吉昌，中。 有鐵。 文城，中。 天祐中更曰屈邑。 有孟門山、石鼓山。 昌寧，中。 有鐵。 呂香，中。本平昌，義寧元年析仵城置，貞觀元年更名。仵城。 中。 有雞山。 隰州隰州大寧郡，下。 本龍泉郡，天寶元年更名。 土貢：胡女布、蜜、蠟燭。 戶萬九千四百五十五，口十三萬四千四百二十。 縣六。 有唐興軍，開元十四年置。北又有渤海軍。莫，緊。本鄚，開元十三年更。有九十九淀。清苑，上。文安，上。貞觀元年省豐利縣入焉。任丘，上。武德五年分鄚置。有通利渠，開元四年，令魚思賢開，以洩陂淀，自縣南五里至城西北入滱，得地二百餘頃。長豐，中。本利豐，開元十年析文安、任丘置，是年更名。唐興。上。本武興，如意元年析河間置。長安四年隸易州，是年，還隸瀛州。神龍元年更名。平州北平郡，下。 有昭義軍，大曆元年置。安陽，緊。武德四年省零泉縣，五年省相縣入焉。西二十里有高平渠，刺史李景引安陽水東流溉田，入廣潤陂，咸亨三年開。鄴，緊。南五里有金鳳渠，引天平渠下流溉田，咸亨三年開。有鐵。湯陰，上。本蕩陰。武德四年析安陽置蕩源縣，隸衞州，六年來屬。貞觀元年更蕩源曰湯陰。林慮，上。武德二年以縣置巖州，五年州廢，來屬。有鐵。有林慮山。堯城，上。天祐三年更曰永定。北四十五里有萬金渠，引漳水入故齊都領渠以溉田，咸亨三年開。臨漳。上。南有菊花渠，自鄴引天平渠水溉田，屈曲經三十里。又北三十里有利物渠，自滏陽下入成安，幷取天平渠水以溉田，皆咸亨四年令李仁綽開。衞州汲郡，望。 聊城，緊。武德四年析置茌平縣，又析魏州之莘置莘亭縣。貞觀元年皆省。天祐三年更曰聊邑，又以聊邑、博平、高唐、武水之河外地入鄆州。東南有四口故關。博平，上。武德三年析置靈泉縣，四年省。貞觀十七年省博平入聊城，天授二年復置。武水，上。清平，上。武德四年置。堂邑，上。 有府六，曰隰川、大義、孝敬、脩善、玉城、屈產。 隰川，中。 蒲，中。武德二年以縣置昌州，幷置仵城、常安、昌原三縣。貞觀元年州廢，省昌原、仵城、常安，以蒲來屬。西南有常安原。大寧，中。本仵城，武德二年更名，是年置中州，幷置大義、白龍二縣。貞觀元年州廢，省大義、白龍，以大寧來屬。有孔山。西有馬鬬關。永和，中。武德二年置東和州，六年析置樓山縣。貞觀二年州廢，省樓山，以永和來屬。西北有永和關。石樓，中。武德二年以縣置西德州，幷置長壽、臨河二縣。貞觀元年州廢，省長壽、臨河，以石樓隸東和州，州廢來屬。北有上平津。溫泉。中。武德三年置北溫州，幷置新城、高唐二縣。貞觀元年州廢，省新城、高唐，以溫泉來屬。有鐵。北都，天授元年置，神龍元年罷，開元十一年復置，天寶元年曰北京，上元二年罷，肅宗元年復為北都。晉陽宮在都之西北，宮城周二千五百二十步，崇四丈八尺。都城左汾右晉，潛丘在中，長四千三百二十一步，廣三千一百二十二步，周萬五千一百五十三步，其崇四丈。汾東曰東城，貞觀十一年長史李勣築。兩城之間有中城，武后時築，以合東城。宮南有大明城，故宮城也。宮城東有起義堂。倉城中有受瑞壇。唐初高祖使子元吉留守，獲瑞石，有文曰「李淵萬吉」，築壇，祠以少牢。太原府太原郡，本幷州，開元十一年為府。 蒲，大寧，永和，石樓，溫泉。 北都北都，天授元年置，神龍元年罷，開元十一年復置，天寶元年曰北京，上元二年罷，肅宗元年復為北都。 太原府太原府太原郡，本幷州，開元十一年為府。 土貢：銅鏡、鐵鏡、馬鞌、梨、蒲萄酒及煎玉粉屑、龍骨、柏實人、黃石𨥥、甘草、人葠、礬石、礜石。 戶十二萬八千九百五，口七十七萬八千二百七十八。 縣十三。 太原，赤。 井苦不可飲，貞觀中，長史李勣架汾引晉水入東城，以甘民食，謂之晉渠。 晉陽，赤。有號令堂，高祖誓義師於此。西北十五里有講武臺、飛閣，顯慶五年築。有龍山。太谷，畿。武德三年以太谷、祁置太州，六年州廢，二縣來屬。東南八十里馬嶺上有長城，自平城至于魯口三百里，貞觀元年廢。祁，畿。文水，畿。武德三年隸汾州，六年來屬，七年又隸汾州，貞觀元年復舊，天授元年更名武興，神龍元年復故名。西北二十里有柵城渠，貞觀三年，民相率引文谷水，溉田數百頃。西十里有常渠，武德二年，汾州刺史蕭顗引文水南流入汾州。東北五十里有甘泉渠，二十五里有蕩沙渠，二十里有靈長渠，有千畝渠俱引文谷水，傳溉田數千頃，皆開元二年令戴謙所鑿。榆次，畿。盂，畿。武德三年以盂、受陽置受州，貞觀元年省并州之烏河縣入焉。有銅、有鐵。東北有白馬故關。壽陽，畿。本受陽。武德六年徙受州來治，又以遼州之石艾、樂平隸之。貞觀八年州廢，縣皆來屬，十一年更名。有方山。樂平，畿。廣陽，畿。本石艾，天寶元年更名。東有井故關。東北有盤石故關、葦澤故關。清源，畿。武德元年置。交城，畿。先天二年析置靈川縣，開元二年省。有鐵。陽曲。畿。本陽直。武德三年析置汾陽縣，七年省陽直，更汾陽曰陽曲，仍析置羅陰縣。貞觀元年省，六年以蘇農部落燕然縣，隸順州，八年僑治陽曲，十七年省。有赤塘關、天門關。汾州西河郡，望。 晉陽，太谷，祁，畿。 文水，榆次，畿。 盂，壽陽，樂平，畿。 廣陽，清源，交城，陽曲。 汾州汾州西河郡，望。 本浩州，武德三年更名。 土貢：鞌面氈、龍鬚席、石膏、消石。 戶五萬九千四百五十，口三十二萬二百三十。 縣五。 有府十二，曰嘉善、六壁、崇德、華夏、靈扶、五柳、京陵、介休、賈胡、寧固、開遠、清勝。 西河，望。 本隰城，肅宗上元年更名。 孝義，望。本永安，貞觀元年更名。有隱泉山。介休，望。義寧元年以介休、平遙置介休郡，武德元年曰介州，貞觀元年州廢，以二縣來屬。有雀鼠谷。有介山。平遙，望。 靈石。 上。 有賈胡堡，宋金剛拒唐兵，高祖所次。 西南有陰地關，又有長寧關。 沁州沁州陽城郡，下。 本義寧郡，義寧元年置，天寶元年更郡名。 土貢：龍鬚席、弦麻。 戶六千三百八，口三萬四千九百六十三。 縣三。 有府二，曰漁陽、臨渠。南二百里有靜塞軍，本障塞軍，開元十九年更名。又有雄武軍，故廣漢川也。東北九十里有洪水守捉，又東北三十里有鹽城守捉，又東北渡灤河有古盧龍鎮，又有斗陘鎮。自古盧龍北經九荊嶺、受米城、張洪隘度石嶺至奚王帳六百里。又東北行傍吐護真河五百里至奚、契丹衙帳。又北百里至室韋帳。漁陽，中。神龍元年隸營州，開元四年還隸幽州。有平虜渠傍海穿漕，以避海難，又其北漲水為溝，以拒契丹，皆神龍中滄州刺史姜師度開。三河，中。開元四年析潞置。北十二里有渠河塘。西北六十里有孤山陂，溉田三千頃。玉田。中。本無終，武德二年置，貞觀元年省，乾封二年復置，萬歲通天元年更名，神龍元年隸營州，開元四年還隸幽州，八年隸營州，十一年又隸幽州。有壕門、米亭、三谷、礓石、方公、白楊等七戍。營州柳城郡，上都督府。 有府一，曰盧龍。有盧龍軍，天寶二載743年置。又有柳城軍，永泰元年置。有溫溝、白望、西狹石、東狹石、綠疇、米磚、長楊、黃花、紫蒙、白狼、昌黎、遼西等十二戍，愛川、周夔二鎮城。東北有明垤關、鶻湖城、牛毛城。盧龍，中。本肥如，武德二年更名，又置撫寧縣，七年省。石城，中。本臨渝，武德七年省，貞觀十五年復置，萬歲通天二年更名。有臨渝關，一名臨閭關。有大海關。有碣石山。有溫昌鎮。馬城。中。古海陽城也，開元二十八年置，以通水運。東北有千金冶。城東有茂鄉鎮城。媯州媯川郡，上。 東北有橫野軍，乾元元年徙天成軍合之，而廢橫野軍。西有清塞軍，本清塞守捉城，貞元十五年置。 有府二，曰延雙、安樂。 沁源，中。武德二年析置招遠縣，三年省。有柴店關。和川，中。義寧元年析沁源置。綿上。 中。 有鐵。 遼州遼州樂平郡，下。 武德三年析并州之樂平、遼山、平城、石艾置，六年徙治遼山，八年曰箕州。 先天元年避玄宗名曰儀州。 中和三年復曰遼州。 土貢：人葰、蠟。 戶九千八百八十二，口五萬四千五百八十。 縣四。 弓高，上。本隸德州，武德四年，以弓高及胡蘇、東光，冀州之阜城、蓨、安陵、觀津置觀州，幷析東光置安陵縣，析蓨置觀津縣。六年以胡蘇隸滄州。貞觀元年省觀津，復以胡蘇隸觀州。十七年州廢，以弓高、東光、胡蘇隸滄州，蓨、安陵隸德州，阜城還隸冀州。東光，上。 有府三，曰遼城、清谷、龍城。 遼山，中。 榆社，中。本隸太原郡，義寧元年析上黨之鄉置。武德元年隸韓州。三年以縣及幷州之平城置榆州，又析置偃武縣。六年州廢，省偃武，以榆社、平城來屬。平城，中。 和順，中。武德三年析置義興縣，六年省。 嵐州樓煩郡，下。 本東會州，武德六年更名。 土貢：熊鞹、麝香。 戶萬六千七百四十八，口八萬四千六。 縣四。 有府一，曰嵐山。 有守捉兵。 宜芳，中。本嵐城，武德四年更名，析置豊閏、合會二縣，五年省豊閏，六年省合會。靜樂，中。武德四年置管州，仍析置汾陽、六度二縣。五年曰北管州。六年州廢，省汾陽、六度，以靜樂來屬。有天池祠。有管涔山。北有樓煩關，有隋故汾陽宮。合河，中。本臨泉。武德三年曰臨津，四年隸東會州，九年省太和縣入焉。貞觀元年更名，三年復置大和，八年又省。北有合河關。東有蔚汾關。嵐谷。中。長安三年析宜芳置，神龍二年省，開元十二年復置。有岢嵐軍，永淳二年以岢嵐鎮為柵，長安三年為軍，景龍中，張仁亶徙其軍於朔方，留者號岢嵐守捉，隸大同。憲州，下。 宜芳，靜樂，合河，嵐谷。 憲州憲州，下。 本樓煩監牧，嵐州刺史領之。 貞元十五年別置監牧使。 龍紀元年，李克用表置州，領縣三。 樓煩，下。 玄池，下。 有鐵。 天池。 下。 有鴈門關。 石州石州昌化郡，下。 本離石郡，天寶元年更名。 土貢：胡女布、龍鬚席、蜜、蠟燭、莁荑。 戶萬四千二百九十四，口六萬六千九百三十五。 縣五。 有府二，曰離石、昌化。 離石，中。 平夷，中。 有孝文山。 定胡，中。武德三年置西定州。貞觀二年州廢，來屬，又析置孟門縣，七年省。西有孟門關。臨泉，中。本太和。武德三年更名，置北和州，別析置太和縣，四年以太和隸東會州。貞觀三年州廢，以臨泉來屬。方山。中。武德二年以縣置方州，三年州廢，來屬。忻州定襄郡，下。 定胡，臨泉，方山。 忻州忻州定襄郡，下。 本新興郡，義寧元年以樓煩郡之秀容置。 土貢：麝香、豹尾。 戶萬四千八百六，口八萬二千三十二。 縣二。 有威武軍，萬歲通天元年置，本漁陽，開元十九年更名。又有鎮遠軍，故黑城川也。有三叉城、橫山城、米城。有大王、北來、保要、鹿固、赤城、邀虜、石子䴚七鎮。有臨河、黃崖二戍。 有府四，曰秀容、高城、漳源、定襄。 有守捉兵。 秀容，上。貞觀五年以思結部落於縣境置懷化縣，隸順州。十二年以懷化隸代州，後省。有繫舟山，有鐵。定襄。上。武德四年析秀容置。有石嶺關。 代州鴈門郡，中都督府。 永興，礬山，龍門，懷安。 潞州上黨郡，大都督府。 土貢：貲布、人葰、石蜜、墨。 戶六萬八千三百九十一，口三十八萬八千六百六十一。 縣十。 有義武軍，建中四年置。西有北平軍，開元中置。安喜，緊。本鮮虞，武德四年更名。義豐，緊。萬歲通天二年以拒契丹更名立節，神龍元年復故名。北平，上。萬歲通天二年以拒契丹更名徇忠，神龍元年復故名。西北有安陽故關。望都，上。武德四年置。曲陽，上。本恆陽，元和十五年更名，是年，又更恆岳曰鎮岳，有岳祠。陘邑，中。本隋昌，武德四年曰唐昌，天寶元年更名。唐，上。 有府一，曰戡黎。 上黨，望。有啟聖宮，本飛龍，玄宗故第，開元十一年置，後又更名。有瑞閣。有五龍山、馬駒山。壺關，上。武德四年析上黨置。長子，緊。 屯留，上。 有三嵕山。 潞城，上。天祐二年更曰潞子。襄垣，上。武德元年以襄垣、黎城、涉、銅鞮、鄉置韓州，貞觀十七年州廢，縣皆來屬。東有井谷故關。黎城，上。天祐二年更曰黎亭。有銅山。東有壺口故關。涉，中。 潞城，襄垣，黎城，涉，中。 有鐵。 銅鞮，上。武德三年析置甲水縣，隸韓州，九年省。永徽六年隸沁州。顯慶四年來屬。武鄉。中。本鄉，武后更名武鄉，神龍元年復故名，尋又曰武鄉。北有昂車關。 澤州高平郡，上。 本長平郡，治濩澤，武德八年徙治端氏，貞觀元年徙治晉城，天寶元年更郡名。 土貢：人葠、石英、野雞。 戶二萬七千八百二十二，口十五萬七千九十。 縣六。 有府五，曰丹川、永固、安平、沁水、白澗。 晉城，上。本丹川，武德元年置建州。三年析丹川置晉城以隸之。六年州廢，隸蓋州，徙蓋州來治。九年省丹川、蓋城入晉城。貞觀元年州廢，以晉城、高平、陵川來屬。天祐二年更曰丹川。南有天井關，一名太行關。端氏，中。 晉城，端氏，中。 有隗山。 陵川，中。 陽城，中。本濩澤，天寶元年更名，天祐二年更曰濩澤。有銅，有錫，有鐵。沁水，中。 高平。 上。本隋長平郡，武德元年曰蓋州，領高平、丹川、陵川三縣，幷析置蓋城縣以隸之。有泫水，一曰丹水，貞元元年，令明濟引入城，號甘泉。有省冤谷，本殺谷，玄宗幸潞州，過之，因更名。北有長平關。
The Hedong Circuit lay within the ancient Jizhou region, covering the Han commanderies of Hedong, Taiyuan, Shangdang, Xihe, Yanmen, and Dai together with the principalities of Julu, Changshan, Zhao, and Guangping. Hezhong, Jiang, Jin, Ci, Xi, Shi, Taiyuan, Fen, Xin, Lu, Ze, Qin, and Liao fell within the Shen asterism division; Dai, Yun, Shuo, Wei, Wu, Xin, Lan, and Xian within the Daliang division. The circuit comprised two superior prefectures, nineteen prefectures, and one hundred ten counties. Its notable mountains were Leishou, Jie, Huo, and Wutai. Its major rivers were the Fen, Qin, Dan, and Lu. Its assessed tribute consisted of cloth and fine ramie textiles. Its presented tribute included cloth, mats, leopard tails, bear hides, and hawk feathers. Hezhong Superior Prefecture (Hedong Commandery designation), chief seat. It was formerly Puzhou, ranked as an upper auxiliary prefecture. In the first year of Yining the administration was at Sangquan; in the third year of Wude it was relocated to Hedong. In the eighth year of Kaiyuan the Central Capital was established and made a superior prefecture; that same year the capital was abolished and it again became a prefecture. In the third year of Qianyuan it was restored as a superior prefecture. Its local tribute products were felt, woven fans, dragon bones, jujubes, and Fengqi pears. It had 70,800 households and a population of 469,213. It administered thirteen counties. It had eighteen military establishments, called Xingzheng, Fuhua, Ningjing, Dongwo, Wuquan, Changning, Zhijie, Fenyang, Jingzhi, Xintong, Jinyuan, Wenyang, Qingding, Fengchuan, Zhumi, Ranghu, Xihu, and Wengu. Within the city it had Tianbing Army, abolished in Kaiyuan year eleven. It had thirty-three military establishments, called Xingle, Deyi, Hubi, Longting, Qingyuan, Yonghe, Taocheng, Huoshan, Fenshui, Shouyang, Shougui, Guiren, Changqu, Yucheng, Tongrun, Baoding, Yanhai, Guichun, Dayang, Yong'an, Fengxin, Yongxing, Youwei, Fenyin, Ganquan, Pingchuan, Anbao, Shimen, Suihua, Tandao, Anyi, Chongyi, and the Six Armies. It also had Yaode Army, established in Qianyuan year two and abolished in Guangde year two. Hedong was second-rank metropolitan. It had the Fangyun Office, which drew water from the river for brewing; it was established in Wude year three and abolished in Zhenguan year ten. To the south was Fengling Pass, established in Shengli year one. It had Li Mountain. Hexi was second-rank metropolitan. In Kaiyuan year eight it was divided from Hedong and established, but was soon abolished. In Qianyuan year three, Chaoyi of Tongzhou was renamed Hexi and came under this prefecture. In Dali year five it was returned to Tongzhou, and Chaoyi and Hedong were divided off to establish it separately. It had Pujin Pass, also called Puban. In Kaiyuan year twelve eight oxen were cast, each ox having a man driving it; beneath the oxen were mountains, all of iron, set on both banks to hold the floating bridge. In year fifteen the River Temple was moved here from Chaoyi. Linjin was second-rank metropolitan. It was originally Sangquan; in Wude year three Wenquan County was divided off and established, and in year nine it was abolished. In Tianbao year thirteen its name was changed. Xie was second-rank metropolitan. It was originally Yuxiang; in Wude year one its name was changed. In Zhenguan year seventeen it was abolished and its territory entered Yuxiang; in year twenty-two it was restored. It had the Salt Pond, and also the Women's Salt Pond. It had the Ziquan Office, established in Qianyuan year one, and had twelve copper caves. Yishi was second-rank metropolitan and had Gu Mountain. Yuxiang was second-rank metropolitan. It was separately established in Wude year one. In Zhenguan year twenty-two it was abolished and its territory entered Xie; in Tianshou year two it was restored. Fifteen li north was the Sushui Canal, opened in Zhenguan year seventeen by the prefect Xue Wanche, who led the Sushui from Wenxi down into Linjin. Yongle was second-rank metropolitan. It was established in Wude year one and originally belonged to Ruizhou; when that province was abolished, it belonged to Dingzhou; in Zhenguan year eight it came under this prefecture; later it again belonged to Guozhou, and in Shenlong year one it was restored to its former status. It had Leishou Mountain. Anyi was second-rank metropolitan. In Yining year one, Anyi, Yuxiang, and Xia formed Anyi Commandery. In Wude year one it was called Yuzhou, and Tongxiang County was also divided off and established. In year three Xingle County was divided from Anyi and established. In Zhenguan year one it was abolished. In year seventeen the province was abolished, Tongxiang was abolished into Wenxi, and Anyi and Xie came under this prefecture. In Zhide year two, Anyi was changed to Yuyi; in Qianyuan year one it belonged to Shaanzhou; in Dali year four its former name was restored; and in Yuanhe year three it came under this prefecture. It had Longchi Palace, established in Kaiyuan year eight. It had salt ponds, which together with Xie's formed the two ponds; in Dali year twelve milk-salt appeared there, and they were given the name Baoying Lingqing Pond. It had a silver office. Baoding was second-rank metropolitan. It was originally Fenyin. In Yining year one, Fenyin and Longmen formed Fenyin Commandery; in Wude year one it was called Taizhou; when the province was abolished, it came under this prefecture. In Kaiyuan year ten a precious tripod was obtained, so the name was changed. It had the Shrine of Houtu. Xiangling was close-ranked. It originally belonged to Jinzhou; in Yuanhe year fourteen it belonged to Jiangzhou, and in Dahe year one it came under this prefecture. Jishan was upper-ranked. Its counties included Hedong, Hexi, Linjin, Xie, and Yishi (secondary metropolitan vicinity), the last having Gushan. Yuxiang, Yongle, Anyi, Baoding, Xiangling, and Jishan were upper-ranked. It had originally been subordinate to Jiang Prefecture and was transferred here in the late Tang. It contains Mount Ji. Wanquan was upper-ranked. It originally belonged to Taizhou. In Wude year three, territory from Jishan, Anyi, Yishi, Fenyin, and Longmen was divided off to establish it. When the province was abolished it belonged to Jiangzhou, and in Dashun year two it came under this prefecture. It had Jie Mountain. Longmen was second-rank metropolitan. In Wude year two Taizhou was moved to govern there, and in year five Wanchun County was divided off and established. In Zhenguan year seventeen the province was abolished, Wanchun was abolished into Longmen, and it belonged to Jiangzhou. At the beginning of Yuanhe it came under this prefecture. It had Longmen Pass. It had the Temple of Gaozu, established during Zhenguan. Thirty li north was Guagushan Weir, built in Zhenguan year ten. Twenty-three li southeast was Shishilu Canal; in year twenty-three the county magistrate Zhangsun Shu dug it, irrigating good fertile fields that yielded ten shi per mu. Twenty-one li west was Ma'anwu Canal, also dug by Shu. It had Longmen Granary, established in Kaiyuan year two. Jinzhou, Pingyang Commandery, was eminent. Wanquan and Longmen. Jin Prefecture (Pingyang Commandery designation), distinguished rank. It was formerly Linfen Commandery and was renamed in the second year of Yining. Its local tribute included candles; it had a Pingyang Bureau alum monopoly. It had 64,836 households and a population of 429,221. It administered eight counties. Pingji was upper-ranked. Two li east was Guangrun Marsh, which drew Taibai Canal to pour into it; twenty li southeast was Bihong. Both were opened by the magistrate Gong Zhiyuan in Yonghui year five to store and release water. Ningjin was close-ranked. It was originally Yingtao; in Tianbao year one its name was changed. The land was dry and saline. Southwest was New Canal; during Shangyuan the magistrate Cheng Chumo led Xiao water into the city to irrigate fields, running more than ten li, and the land became rich and moist, so the people's food became sweet. Zhaoqing was eminent. It was originally Dalu; in Wude year four it was called Xiangcheng, and in Tianbao year one its name was changed. Twenty li southwest were Jianchu Mausoleum and Qiyun Mausoleum, the two mausoleums sharing one cemetery. Below the city was Fengshui Canal; in Yifeng year three the magistrate Li Xuan opened it to irrigate fields and connect transport. Baixiang was upper-ranked. Longgang was upper-ranked. In Wude year one Qingshan County was divided from Longgang and Neiqiu and established; in Kaicheng year five it was abolished into Longgang. Shahe was upper-ranked. In Wude year one Wenzhou was established; in year four the province was abolished and it came under this prefecture. It had iron. Nanhe was close-ranked. In Wude year one Hezhou was established; in year four the province was abolished and it came under this prefecture. Julu was upper-ranked. In Wude year one Qizhou was established, and Baiqi County was also divided off and established. In year four the province was abolished, Baiqi was abolished, and Julu belonged to Zhaozhou. In Zhenguan year one it came under this prefecture. It had Dalu Marsh. It had salty springs, boiled to make salt. Pingxiang was upper-ranked. In Wude year one Fengzhou was established; in year four the province was abolished and it came under this prefecture. During Zhenyuan, the prefect Yuan Yi shifted the Zhang River so that it emerged twenty li east of the prefectural seat and entered the old river ten li north of Julu. Ren was middle-ranked. It was established in Wude year four. Yaoshan was upper-ranked. It was originally Bairen. In Wude year one Eastern Longzhou was established; in year four the province was abolished and it belonged to Zhaozhou; in year five it came under this prefecture. In Tianbao year one its name was changed. Neiqiu was upper-ranked. In Wude year four it belonged to Zhaozhou, and in year five it came under this prefecture. It had iron. Mingzhou, Guangping Commandery, was eminent. It had fifteen garrison commands: Shenshan, Pingyang, Fengning, Jicheng, Anxin, Wan'an, Yichang, Yingtai, Yueyang, Renshou, Gaoyang, Linfen, Jin'an, Baizhuang, Gaohua, and Rende. Linfen was eminent. Ten li northeast was Gaoliang Weir, which during Wude drew Gaoliang water to irrigate fields and entered Baijin Marsh. In Zhenguan year thirteen it was destroyed by water. In Yonghui year two the prefect Li Kuan led Jue water from Xiachai Weir twenty-five li to the east to irrigate fields, and ordered Tao Shanding to restore Baijin Marsh, also drawing Jue water to irrigate fields. In Qianfeng year two the weir collapsed, so Jin water was led from the west. It had Gushe Mountain. Hongdong was eminent. It was originally Yang, and in Yining year two its name was changed. In Wude year one, Xihe County was divided from Hongdong and Linfen and established; in Zhenguan year seventeen it was abolished into Linfen. Shenshan was middle-ranked. It was originally Fushan; in Wude year two it was divided from Xiangling and established. To the southeast it had Yangjiao Mountain. In year four its name was changed because of the Shrine of Laozi. Yueyang was middle-ranked. Linfen, Hongtong, Shenshan, and Yueyang were middle-ranked. To its east lay the garrison-city pass. It had iron deposits. Wenxi was eminent. It was established in Wude year one. It had copper smelteries. Thirty-five li southeast was Sha Canal; in Yifeng year two an edict ordered water from Zhongtiao Mountain to be drawn below the southern slope, flowing west for sixteen li to irrigate fields south of the Su. Yuan was upper-ranked. In Yining year one, Yuan and Wangwu formed Shaoyuan Commandery, and Qinglian and Bocheng counties were also established. In Wude year one it was called Shaozhou. In year two Changquan County was established; that year Changquan was assigned to Huaizhou and was later abolished. In year five Bocheng was abolished into Yuan. In Zhenguan year one the province was abolished, Qinglian was abolished into Yuan, and it came under this prefecture. In Longshuo year two it belonged to Luozhou, in Chang'an year two its former status was restored; in Zhenyuan year three it belonged to Shaanzhou, and in Yuanhe year three its former status was restored. Cizhou, Wencheng Commandery, was lower-ranked. Huoyi was upper-ranked. In Yining year one, Huoyi, Zhaocheng, Fenxi, and Lingshi formed Huoshan Commandery. In Wude year one it was called Luzhou. In Zhenguan year seventeen the province was abolished; Lingshi belonged to Fenzhou, while Huoyi, Zhaocheng, and Fenxi came under this prefecture. It had the Shrine of Huoshan of the Northwest Marchmount. Zhaocheng was upper-ranked. In Yining year one it was divided from Huoyi and established. Fenxi was middle-ranked. Huoyi, Zhaocheng, and Fenxi were middle-ranked. They had iron deposits. Jishi. Middle rank. Jiang Prefecture (Jiang Commandery designation), powerful rank. Its local tribute included white silk gauze, millet, pears, ink, candles, and saposhnikovia root. It had 82,204 households and a population of 517,331. It administered seven counties. Southwest was Henghai Army, established in Kaiyuan year fourteen, abolished after Tianbao, and restored in Dali year one. Qingchi was close-ranked. Fifty-five li northwest were two Yongji dikes, built in Yonghui year two. Forty-five li west were two Minggou River dikes, and fifty li west were the eastern dike of Libiao Marsh and the western dike of the Tuhai River, all built in year three. Forty li west were two Hengzhang dikes, built in Xianqing year one. Sixty li northwest was the eastern dike of the Hengzhang, built in Kaiyuan year ten. Twenty li southeast was a canal pouring into the Maoshi River, and seventy li southeast was a canal pouring into the Zhang; both drew Fu water and were opened by the prefect Jiang Shidu. Fifty-seven li southwest was the Wudi River, and fifteen li southeast was the Yangtong River, both opened in Kaiyuan year sixteen. Fifteen li south were the Fu River Dike and the Yangtong River Dike, and thirty li farther south was the northern dike of Yongji, also built that year. It had two sweet wells; in year ten, because the magistrate Mao's mother was elderly and the bitter, salty water gave him no way to support her, the ground at the county office was dug, and a spring gushed out sweet; the people called it Lord Mao's Well. It had salt. Yanshan was close-ranked. In Wude year four Eastern Yanzhou was established. In year five, Qingchi of Jingzhou was combined with territory divided from Yanshan to establish Fushui County, which belonged to it. In Zhenguan year one the province was abolished, Fushui was abolished, and Qingchi and Yanshan came under this prefecture. It had salt. Changlu was upper-ranked. It originally belonged to Yingzhou. In Wude year four, Jingzhou was established from Changlu, Pingshu, Lucheng, and Qingchi of Cangzhou. In Zhenguan year one the province was abolished; Pingshu returned to Yingzhou, and Changlu and Lucheng came under this prefecture. Leling was upper-ranked. It originally belonged to Dizhou; in Wude year eight it came under this prefecture, in Dahe year two it again belonged to Dizhou, and soon again came under this prefecture. Rao'an was upper-ranked. In Wude year four Gejin County was divided off and established; in Zhenguan year one it was abolished into Leling. Wudi was upper-ranked. In Zhenguan year one it was abolished into Yangxin, in year eight it was restored, in Dahe year two it belonged to Dizhou, and soon came under this prefecture. It had Wudi Canal connecting to the sea; it was abandoned at the end of Sui, and in Yonghui year one the prefect Xue Dading opened it. Qianfu was upper-ranked. It was originally Lucheng. In Qianfu year one wild rice grew in more than two thousand qing of water-grain fields, and famine refugees from Yan and Wei went there to eat, so its name was changed. Jingzhou was upper-ranked. Luze was upper-ranked. In Xiantian year two it was divided from Raoyang and Lucheng and established. Raoyang was eminent. In Wude year four Wulou County was divided off and established; in Zhenguan year one it was abolished. Shulu was upper-ranked. It was originally Lucheng; in Tianbao year fifteen its name was changed. Anping was upper-ranked. Boye was eminent. It originally belonged to Manzhou. In Wude year five, Lizhou was established from Boye, Qingyuan, and Yifeng of Dingzhou; in year eight the province was abolished and the counties returned to their former jurisdictions; in year nine it was again established from Boye and Qingyuan. In Zhenguan year one the province was abolished, and Boye and Qingyuan belonged to Yingzhou. During Yongtai, Boye came under this prefecture. In Yuanhe year ten it again belonged to Yingzhou, and later again came under this prefecture. Leshou was close-ranked. It originally belonged to Yingzhou; during Dali it came under this prefecture; in Yuanhe year ten it again belonged to Yingzhou, and later again came under this prefecture. Xiabo was upper-ranked. It originally belonged to Jizhou; in Zhenguan year one it came under this prefecture. When the province was abolished, it returned to Jizhou. Later it again came under this prefecture. In Kaiyuan year two it belonged to Jizhou. In Yongtai year one it again came under this prefecture. It had Yongning Army, established in Zhenyuan year ten. Zhaozhou, Zhao Commandery, was eminent. It had thirty-three garrison commands: Xintian, Taiping, Zhengping, Wucheng, Changshe, Daxiang, Yuancheng, Shuchuan, Jiangchuan, Gaisong, Fengting, Yanguang, Pingyuan, Gaoliang, Shenquan, Tongxiang, Wanquan, Yicheng, Pishi, Dongze, Lingyuan, Shichi, Yanfu, Yongkang, Jingshan, Zhouyang, Xiatai, Guting, Chongle, Jiangyi, Changping, Wuyang, and Puyi. Zhengping was distinguished rank. To its west lay the former Wuping Pass. Taiping was close-ranked. It had Taiping Pass, established in Zhenguan year seven. Quwo was eminent. Thirty-five li northeast was Xinjiang Canal; in Yonghui year one the magistrate Cui Yi drew Gudui water to irrigate more than one hundred qing of fields. In the mountains thirteen li south there was copper. Yicheng was eminent. In Yining year one, Yicheng and Jiang formed Yicheng Commandery, and Xiaoxiang County was also established. In Wude year one it was called Huizhou; in year two it was called Northern Huizhou; in year four the province was abolished and all the counties came under this prefecture; in year nine Xiaoxiang was abolished into Yicheng. In Tianyou year two its name was changed to Huichuan. It had two mints, Tongyuan and Xianggao. It had Huigao Mountain, copper, and iron. Jiang was eminent. Taiping, Quwo, Yicheng, and Jiang were distinguished rank. They had iron deposits. Wenxi and Yuan. Ci Prefecture (Wencheng Commandery designation), lower rank. It was formerly Fen Prefecture; in the fifth year of Wude it was called South Fen Prefecture and was renamed in the eighth year of Zhenguan. Its local tribute included white honey and candles. It had 11,616 households and a population of 62,486. It administered five counties. Hejian was eminent. In Wude year five Wuyuan County was established, and in Zhenguan year one it was abolished into Hejian. One hundred li northwest was Changfeng Canal, opened by the prefect Zhu Tan in year twenty-one. Five li southwest was also Changfeng Canal; in Kaiyuan year twenty-five the prefect Lu Hui led the Hutuo from Shucheng and Pingshu eastward into the Qi to connect water transport and irrigate more than five hundred qing of fields. Gaoyang was upper-ranked. In Wude year four Manzhou was established from Gaoyang, Mo, Boye, and Qingyuan. In year five Boye and Qingyuan were assigned to Lizhou. In Zhenguan year one the province was abolished, and Mo and Gaoyang came under this prefecture. Pingshu was upper-ranked. Ji was close-ranked. In Wude year one Yizhou was established from Ji and Xinxiang. In year four the province was abolished; Ji came under this prefecture, and Xinxiang belonged to Yinzhou. Wei was close-ranked. In Zhenguan year seventeen Qingqi County was abolished into it. In Chang'an year three Qingqi County was restored, and in Shenlong year one it was again abolished. On the Yu River there was one stone weir, built in Zhenguan year seventeen. It had Sumen Mountain. Gongcheng was upper-ranked. In Wude year one Gongzhou was established from the county, and Fancheng County was also divided off and established. In year four the province was abolished, Fancheng was abolished, and Gongcheng belonged to Yinzhou. In year six Bowang County was abolished into it. It had Bailu Mountain. Xinxiang was eminent. It had Heyang Army, established in Jianzhong year four. Heyang was eminent. In Wude year four, Heyang, Jicheng, and Wen of Huaizhou were divided off at Heyang Palace to establish Mengzhou. In year eight the province was abolished, Jicheng was abolished into Heyang, and Wen belonged to Huaizhou. In Xianqing year two it belonged to Luozhou. It had Heyang Pass. It had the old city of Huiluo. It had a pond; in Yonghui year four Ji River water was led in to fill it, and during Kaiyuan it was used to raise yellow fish. Sishui was eminent. It originally belonged to Zhengzhou. In Wude year four Chenggao County was divided off and established; in Zhenguan year one it was abolished; in Xianqing year two it belonged to Luozhou; in Chuigong year four it was called Guangwu; and in Shenlong year one its former name was restored. It had Hulao Pass. To the southeast was the old Chenggao Pass. To the southwest was the old Xuanmen Pass. It had Niukou Isle. One li west, on Fugui Mountain, was Zhaowu Temple, established in Huichang year five. Heyin was eminent. In Kaiyuan year twenty-two it was divided from Sishui, Yingze, and Wuzhi and established; it belonged to Henan Prefecture and governed Heyin Granary, and in Huichang year three it came under this prefecture. It had Duke Liang's Weir, between the Yellow River and the Bian; in Kaiyuan year two Li Jie, governor of Henan, dredged it along an old canal to facilitate water transport. Wen was eminent. In Wude year four the Sui magistrate Zhou Zhongyin brought the county away from Wang Shichong and surrendered; Pingzhou was established, and the county town was named Li City. That year the province was abolished and it belonged to Huaizhou. In Xianqing year two it belonged to Luozhou. Jiyuan was eminent. In Wude year two Wang Shichong's general Ding Bode surrendered with the county; Western Jizhou was established, and Xiuyang, Zhengchuan, and Shaoyuan counties were also divided off and established. In year four the province was abolished, Xiuyang, Zhengchuan, and Shaoyuan were abolished, and Jiyuan belonged to Huaizhou. In Zhenguan year one Zhi County of Huaizhou was abolished into it. In Xianqing year two it belonged to Luozhou. It had Fangkou Weir; in Dahe year five the military governor Wen Zao dredged an old canal, irrigating five thousand qing of fields in Jiyuan, Henei, Wen, and Wuzhi. It had the Shrine of Jidu and the Shrine of Beihai. To the west was the old Zhi Pass. Huaizhou, Henei Commandery, was strong. It had three military establishments, called Wutai, Dongye, and Yanmen. It had garrison troops. To its north was Datong Army, originally Dawu Army; in Diaolu year two it was called Shenwu Army, in Tianshou year two it was called Pingdi Army, and in Dazu year one its name was again changed. To its west was Tian'an Army, established in Tianbao year twelve. It also had Daibei Army, established in Yongtai year one. It had three garrison commands: Wucheng, Jichang, and Pingchang. Jichang was middle rank. It had iron deposits. Wencheng was middle rank. During the Tianyou era it was renamed Quyi. It had Mount Mengmen and Mount Shigu. Changning was middle rank. It had iron deposits. Luxiang, originally Pingchang, was a middle-ranked county created from Wucheng in Yining 1 and renamed in Zhenguan 1. Wucheng followed. Middle rank. It had Mount Ji. Xi Prefecture (Daning Commandery designation), lower rank. It was formerly Longquan Commandery and was renamed in the first year of Tianbao. Its local tribute included Hu-woman cloth, honey, and candles. It had 19,455 households and a population of 134,420. It administered six counties. It had Tangxing Army, established in Kaiyuan year fourteen. To the north it also had Bohai Army. Mo was close-ranked. It was originally Mo; in Kaiyuan year thirteen its name was changed. It had ninety-nine marshes. Qingyuan was upper-ranked. Wen'an was upper-ranked. In Zhenguan year one Fengli County was abolished into it. Renqiu was upper-ranked. In Wude year five it was divided from Mo and established. It had Tongli Canal, opened by the magistrate Yu Sixian in Kaiyuan year four to drain embanked marshes; from five li south of the county to northwest of the city it entered the Kou, gaining more than two hundred qing of land. Changfeng was middle-ranked. It was originally Lifeng; in Kaiyuan year ten it was divided from Wen'an and Renqiu and established, and that year its name was changed. Tangxing was upper-ranked. It was originally Wuxing; in Ruyi year one it was divided from Hejian and established. In Chang'an year four it belonged to Yizhou; that year it was returned to Yingzhou. In Shenlong year one its name was changed. Pingzhou, Beiping Commandery, was lower-ranked. It had Zhaoyi Army, established in Dali year one. Anyang was close-ranked. In Wude year four Lingquan County was abolished, and in year five Xiang County was abolished into it. Twenty li west was Gaoping Canal; the prefect Li Jing led Anyang water eastward to irrigate fields and enter Guangrun Marsh, opening it in Xianheng year three. Ye was close-ranked. Five li south was Jinfeng Canal, which drew the lower flow of Tianping Canal to irrigate fields; it was opened in Xianheng year three. It had iron. Tangyin was upper-ranked. It was originally Dangyin. In Wude year four Dangyuan County was divided from Anyang and established, belonging to Weizhou; in year six it came under this prefecture. In Zhenguan year one Dangyuan was changed to Tangyin. Linlü was upper-ranked. In Wude year two Yanzhou was established from the county; in year five the province was abolished and it came under this prefecture. It had iron. It had Linlü Mountain. Yaocheng was upper-ranked. In Tianyou year three it was changed to Yongding. Forty-five li north was Wanjin Canal, which led Zhang water into the old Qidu Supervisory Canal to irrigate fields; it was opened in Xianheng year three. Linzhang was upper-ranked. To the south was Juhua Canal, which drew Tianping Canal water from Ye to irrigate fields, winding for thirty li. Thirty li north was also Liwu Canal, which ran down from Fuyang into Cheng'an and likewise took Tianping Canal water to irrigate fields; both were opened by the magistrate Li Renchuo in Xianheng year four. Weizhou, Ji Commandery, was eminent. Liaocheng was close-ranked. In Wude year four Chiping County was divided off and established, and Xinting County was also divided from Shen of Weizhou and established. In Zhenguan year one both were abolished. In Tianyou year three its name was changed to Liaoyi, and the territory of Liaoyi, Boping, Gaotang, and Wushui beyond the Yellow River was also put into Yunzhou. To the southeast was the old Sikou Pass. Boping was upper-ranked. In Wude year three Lingquan County was divided off and established, and in year four it was abolished. In Zhenguan year seventeen Boping was abolished into Liaocheng, and in Tianshou year two it was restored. Wushui was upper-ranked. Qingping was upper-ranked. It was established in Wude year four. Tangyi was upper-ranked. It had six garrison commands: Xichuan, Dayi, Xiaojing, Xiushan, Yucheng, and Quchan. Xichuan was middle rank. Pu was middle-ranked. In Wude year two, Changzhou was established from the county, and Wucheng, Chang'an, and Changyuan counties were also established. In Zhenguan year one the province was abolished; Changyuan, Wucheng, and Chang'an were abolished, and Pu came under this prefecture. Southwest it had Chang'an Plain. Daning was middle-ranked. It was originally Wucheng; in Wude year two its name was changed, and that year Zhongzhou was established, together with Dayi and Bailong counties. In Zhenguan year one the province was abolished; Dayi and Bailong were abolished, and Daning came under this prefecture. It had Kong Mountain. To the west was Madou Pass. Yonghe was middle-ranked. In Wude year two Donghezhou was established, and in year six Loushan County was divided off and established. In Zhenguan year two the province was abolished; Loushan was abolished, and Yonghe came under this prefecture. To the northwest was Yonghe Pass. Shilou was middle-ranked. In Wude year two Xidezhou was established from the county, and Changshou and Linhe counties were also established. In Zhenguan year one the province was abolished; Changshou and Linhe were abolished, and Shilou belonged to Donghezhou; when that province was abolished, it came under this prefecture. To the north was Shangping Ford. Wenquan was middle-ranked. In Wude year three Northern Wenzhou was established, together with Xincheng and Gaotang counties. In Zhenguan year one the province was abolished; Xincheng and Gaotang were abolished, and Wenquan came under this prefecture. It had iron. The Northern Capital was established in Tianshou year one, abolished in Shenlong year one, restored in Kaiyuan year eleven, called Beijing in Tianbao year one, abolished in Shangyuan year two, and restored as Northern Capital in Suzong's first year. Jinyang Palace lay northwest of the capital. The palace wall measured 2,520 paces around and was four zhang eight chi high. The capital city had the Fen on its left and the Jin on its right, with Qian Hill in its center; it was 4,321 paces long, 3,122 paces wide, and 15,153 paces around, and its height was four zhang. East of the Fen was called the Eastern City, built by the senior administrator Li Ji in Zhenguan year eleven. Between the two cities was the Middle City, built in Empress Wu's time to join the Eastern City. South of the palace was Daming City, the old palace city. East of the palace city was the Hall of Raising Righteousness. Inside the granary city was the Altar for Receiving Auspicious Signs. At the beginning of Tang, Gaozu had his son Yuanji remain as garrison commander; when an auspicious stone was found, its inscription read, "Li Yuan, ten thousand auspiciousnesses." An altar was built, and sacrifices were offered with the lesser victim. Taiyuan Prefecture, Taiyuan Commandery, was originally Bingzhou; in Kaiyuan year eleven it became a prefecture. Pu, Daning, Yonghe, Shilou, and Wenquan. The Northern Capital was established in the first year of Tianshou, abolished in the first year of Shenlong, restored in the eleventh year of Kaiyuan, renamed Beijing in the first year of Tianbao, abolished in the second year of Shangyuan, and restored as the Northern Capital in the first year of Suzong. Taiyuan Superior Prefecture (Taiyuan Commandery designation) was originally Bing Prefecture and became a superior prefecture in the eleventh year of Kaiyuan. Its local tribute included bronze mirrors, iron mirrors, saddles, pears, grape wine, ground jade powder, dragon bones, cypress fruit kernels, yellow stone ore, licorice, ginseng, alum, and arsenic ore. It had 128,905 households and a population of 778,278. It administered thirteen counties. Taiyuan was chief rank. The city wells yielded bitter, undrinkable water; during the Zhenguan era Chief Administrator Li Ji built an aqueduct from the Fen River to channel Jin River water into the eastern city for the people's drinking supply, known as the Jin Canal. Jinyang was metropolitan. It had the Hall of Commands, where Gaozu swore in the righteous army. Fifteen li northwest were the Military Instruction Terrace and the Flying Gallery, built in Xianqing year five. It had Long Mountain. Taigu was metropolitan. In Wude year three, Taizhou was established from Taigu and Qi; in year six the province was abolished, and the two counties came under this prefecture. Eighty li southeast, on Maling, there was a long wall stretching three hundred li from Pingcheng to Lukou; it was abolished in Zhenguan year one. Qi was metropolitan. Wenshui was metropolitan. In Wude year three it belonged to Fenzhou, in year six it came under this prefecture, in year seven it again belonged to Fenzhou, and in Zhenguan year one its former status was restored. In Tianshou year one its name was changed to Wuxing, and in Shenlong year one its former name was restored. Twenty li northwest was Zhacheng Canal; in Zhenguan year three the people together drew Wengu water to irrigate several hundred qing of fields. Ten li west was Chang Canal; in Wude year two Xiao Yi, prefect of Fenzhou, led Wenshui south into Fenzhou. Fifty li northeast was Ganquan Canal, twenty-five li northeast was Dangsha Canal, twenty li northeast was Lingchang Canal, and there was also Qianmu Canal; all drew Wengu water and passed it on to irrigate several thousand qing of fields, and all were dug by the magistrate Dai Qian in Kaiyuan year two. Yuci was metropolitan. Yu was metropolitan. In Wude year three, Shouzhou was established from Yu and Shouyang; in Zhenguan year one Wuhe County of Bingzhou was abolished into it. It had copper and iron. To the northeast was the old Baima Pass. Shouyang was metropolitan. It was originally Shouyang. In Wude year six Shouzhou was moved to govern there, and Shiai and Leping of Liaozhou were also assigned to it. In Zhenguan year eight the province was abolished and all the counties came under this prefecture; in year eleven its name was changed. It had Fang Mountain. Leping was metropolitan. Guangyang was metropolitan. It was originally Shiai; in Tianbao year one its name was changed. To the east was the old Jing Pass. To the northeast were the old Panshi Pass and Weize Pass. Qingyuan was metropolitan. It was established in Wude year one. Jiaocheng was metropolitan. In Xiantian year two Lingchuan County was divided off and established; in Kaiyuan year two it was abolished. It had iron. Yangqu was metropolitan. It was originally Yangzhi. In Wude year three Fenyang County was divided off and established; in year seven Yangzhi was abolished, Fenyang was changed to Yangqu, and Luoyin County was still divided off and established. In Zhenguan year one it was abolished. In year six, Yanran County of the Sunong tribes was assigned to Shunzhou; in year eight it was lodged at Yangqu, and in year seventeen it was abolished. It had Chitang Pass and Tianmen Pass. Fenzhou, Xihe Commandery, was eminent. Jinyang, Taigu, and Qi were metropolitan vicinity rank. Wenshui and Yuci were metropolitan vicinity rank. Yu, Shouyang, and Leping were metropolitan vicinity rank. Guangyang, Qingyuan, Jiaocheng, and Yangqu. Fen Prefecture (Xihe Commandery designation), distinguished rank. It was formerly Haozhou and was renamed in the third year of Wude. Its local tribute included saddle-face felt, dragon-whisker mats, gypsum, and saltpeter. It had 59,450 households and a population of 320,230. It administered five counties. It had twelve garrison commands: Jiashan, Liubi, Chongde, Huaxia, Lingfu, Wuliu, Jingling, Jiexiu, Jiahu, Ninggu, Kaiyuan, and Qingsheng. Xihe was distinguished rank. It was formerly Xicheng and was renamed in the first year of Suzong's Shangyuan era. Xiaoyi, Jiexiu, and Pingyao are restored with their ranks, former names, brief prefectural history, and mountain notes. Lingshi. Upper rank. It had Jiahu Fort, where Song Jingang resisted the Tang armies and where Emperor Gaozu made his camp. To its southwest were Yindi Pass and Changning Pass. Qin Prefecture (Yangcheng Commandery designation), lower rank. It was formerly Yining Commandery, established in the first year of Yining; the commandery designation was changed in the first year of Tianbao. Its local tribute included dragon-whisker mats and hemp cord. It had 6,308 households and a population of 34,963. It administered three counties. It had two military establishments, called Yuyang and Linqu. Two hundred li south was Jingsai Army, originally Zhangsai Army; in Kaiyuan year nineteen its name was changed. It also had Xiongwu Army, the old Guanghanchuan. Ninety li northeast was Hongshui Garrison, thirty li farther northeast was Yancheng Garrison, and farther northeast across the Luan River was old Lulong Fortified Town, as well as Douxing Fortified Town. From old Lulong north through Jiujing Ridge, Shoumi City, and Zhanghong Pass, crossing Shiling, to the tent of the Xi king was six hundred li. Traveling farther northeast along Tuhuzhen River for five hundred li reached the administrative tents of the Xi and Khitan. Another one hundred li north reached the Shiwei tents. Yuyang was middle-ranked. In Shenlong year one it belonged to Yingzhou, and in Kaiyuan year four it was returned to Youzhou. It had Pinglu Canal, which cut a transport route alongside the sea to avoid the dangers of the sea, and north of it the swollen water formed a ditch to resist the Khitan; both were opened during Shenlong by Jiang Shidu, prefect of Cangzhou. Sanhe was middle-ranked. In Kaiyuan year four it was divided from Lu and established. Twelve li north was Quhe Pond. Sixty li northwest was Gushan Embankment, irrigating three thousand qing of fields. Yutian was middle-ranked. It was originally Wuzhong; it was established in Wude year two, abolished in Zhenguan year one, restored in Qianfeng year two, renamed in Wansui Tongtian year one, belonged to Yingzhou in Shenlong year one, returned to Youzhou in Kaiyuan year four, belonged to Yingzhou in year eight, and again belonged to Youzhou in year eleven. It had seven garrisons, including Haomen, Miting, Sangu, Jiangshi, Fanggong, and Baiyang. Yingzhou, Liucheng Commandery, was an upper-ranked area command. It had one military establishment, called Lulong. It had Lulong Army, established in Tianbao year two, 743. It also had Liucheng Army, established in Yongtai year one. It had twelve garrisons, Wengou, Baiwang, Western Xiashi, Eastern Xiashi, Luchou, Mizhuan, Changyang, Huanghua, Zimeng, Bailang, Changli, Liaoxi, and others, and two fortified towns, Aichuan and Zhoukui. To the northeast were Mingdie Pass, Huhu City, and Niumao City. Lulong was middle-ranked. It was originally Feiru; in Wude year two its name was changed, and Funing County was also established; in year seven it was abolished. Shicheng was middle-ranked. It was originally Linyu; in Wude year seven it was abolished, in Zhenguan year fifteen it was restored, and in Wansui Tongtian year two its name was changed. It had Linyu Pass, also called Linlü Pass. It had Dahai Pass. It had Jieshi Mountain. It had Wenchang Fortified Town. Macheng was middle-ranked. It was the ancient Haiyang City; in Kaiyuan year twenty-eight it was established to connect water transport. Northeast it had Qianjin Smeltery. East of the city was Maoxiang Fortified Town. Guizhou, Guichuan Commandery, was upper-ranked. To the northeast was Hengye Army; in Qianyuan year one Tiancheng Army was moved to join it, and Hengye Army was abolished. To the west was Qingsai Army, originally Qingsai Garrison City, established in Zhenyuan year fifteen. It had two garrison commands: Yanshuang and Anle. Qinyuan now includes the short-lived Zhaoyuan County and Chaidian Pass; Hechuan was created from Qinyuan in Yining 1. Mianshang followed. Middle rank. It had iron deposits. Liao Prefecture, Leping Commandery designation, lower rank. In the third year of Wude it was carved out of Leping, Liaoshan, Pingcheng, and Shi'ai in Bing Prefecture; in the sixth year the seat moved to Liaoshan; in the eighth year it was named Ji Prefecture. In the first year of Xiantian it was renamed Yi Prefecture to avoid the personal name of Emperor Xuanzong. In the third year of Zhonghe it reverted to the name Liao Prefecture. Its local tribute included ginseng and wax. It had 9,882 households and a population of 54,580. It administered four counties. Gonggao was upper-ranked. It originally belonged to Dezhou. In Wude year four, Guanzhou was established from Gonggao, Husu, Dongguang, Fucheng, Tiao, Anling, and Guanjin of Jizhou, while Anling County was divided from Dongguang and established, and Guanjin County was divided from Tiao and established. In year six Husu belonged to Cangzhou. In Zhenguan year one Guanjin was abolished, and Husu was again assigned to Guanzhou. In year seventeen the province was abolished; Gonggao, Dongguang, and Husu belonged to Cangzhou, Tiao and Anling belonged to Dezhou, and Fucheng returned to Jizhou. Dongguang was upper-ranked. It had three garrison commands: Liaocheng, Qinggu, and Longcheng. Liaoshan was middle rank. Yushe and Pingcheng now preserve the Yining creation of Yushe, the brief Yu Prefecture, the Yanwu County episode, and their middle rank. Heshun was middle-ranked; Yixing County was briefly split from it and then abolished. Lan Prefecture, Loufan Commandery, was lower-ranked. It was formerly East Huizhou and was renamed in the sixth year of Wude. Its local tribute included bear hides and musk. It had 16,748 households and a population of 84,006. It administered four counties. It had one garrison command: Lanshan. It maintained frontier garrison troops. Yifang was middle-ranked. It was originally Lancheng; in Wude year four its name was changed, and Fengrun and Hehui counties were divided off and established. In year five Fengrun was abolished, and in year six Hehui was abolished. Jingle was middle-ranked. In Wude year four Guanzhou was established, and Fenyang and Liudu counties were still divided off and established. In year five it was called Northern Guanzhou. In year six the province was abolished, Fenyang and Liudu were abolished, and Jingle came under this prefecture. It had the Shrine of Tianchi. It had Guancen Mountain. To the north was Loufan Pass, and there was the old Sui Fenyang Palace. Hehe was middle-ranked. It was originally Linquan. In Wude year three it was called Linjin; in year four it belonged to East Huizhou, and in year nine Taihe County was abolished into it. In Zhenguan year one its name was changed; in year three Dahe was restored, and in year eight it was again abolished. To the north was Hehe Pass. To the east was Weifen Pass. Langu was middle-ranked. In Chang'an year three it was divided from Yifang and established, in Shenlong year two it was abolished, and in Kaiyuan year twelve it was restored. It had Kelan Army. In Yongchun year two, Kelan Garrison became a stockade; in Chang'an year three it became an army; during Jinglong, Zhang Rendan moved that army to Shuofang, and those who remained were called Kelan Garrison and belonged to Datong. Xianzhou was lower-ranked. Yifang, Jingle, Hehe, and Langu. Xian Prefecture, lower rank. It was originally the Loufan Pasturage Office, overseen by the prefect of Lan Prefecture. In the fifteenth year of Zhenyuan a separate Pasturage Commissioner was installed. In the first year of Longji, Li Keyong petitioned to establish the prefecture, administering three counties. Loufan was lower rank. Xuanchi was lower rank. It had iron deposits. Tianchi. Lower rank. It had Yanmen Pass. Shi Prefecture, Changhua Commandery designation, lower rank. It was formerly Lishi Commandery and was renamed in the first year of Tianbao. Its local tribute included Hu-woman cloth, dragon-whisker mats, honey, candles, and wuyi herb. It had 14,294 households and a population of 66,935. It administered five counties. It had two garrison commands: Lishi and Changhua. Lishi was middle rank. Pingyi was middle rank. It had Mount Xiaowen. Dinghu was middle-ranked. In Wude year three Western Dingzhou was established. In Zhenguan year two the province was abolished and it came under this prefecture; Mengmen County was also divided off and established, and in year seven it was abolished. To the west was Mengmen Pass. Linquan was middle-ranked. It was originally Taihe. In Wude year three its name was changed and Northern Hezhou was established, while Taihe County was separately divided off and established. In year four Taihe belonged to East Huizhou. In Zhenguan year three the province was abolished, and Linquan came under this prefecture. Fangshan was middle-ranked. In Wude year two Fangzhou was established from the county; in year three the province was abolished and it came under this prefecture. Xinzhou, Dingxiang Commandery, was lower-ranked. Dinghu, Linquan, and Fangshan. Xin Prefecture, Dingxiang Commandery designation, lower rank. It was formerly Xinxing Commandery; in the first year of Yining it was established from Xiurong in Loufan Commandery. Its local tribute included musk and leopard tails. It had 14,806 households and a population of 82,032. It administered two counties. It had Weiwu Army, established in Wansui Tongtian year one; it was originally Yuyang, and in Kaiyuan year nineteen its name was changed. It also had Zhenyuan Army, the old Heichengchuan. It had Sancha City, Hengshan City, and Mi City. It had seven fortified towns: Dawang, Beilai, Baoyao, Lugu, Chicheng, Yaolu, and Shizijian. It had two garrisons, Linhe and Huangya. It had four garrison commands: Xiurong, Gaocheng, Zhangyuan, and Dingxiang. It maintained frontier garrison troops. Xiurong and Dingxiang now include their ranks, Huaihua County for the Sijie tribe, Mount Xizhou, iron, and Shiling Pass. Dai Prefecture, Yanmen Commandery, was a middle-ranked area command. Its local tribute included honey, green glaze pigments, musk, leopard tails, and white hawk feathers. It had 21,280 households and a population of 100,350. It administered five counties. Yanmen was upper rank. It had East Xing Pass and West Xing Pass. Wutai was middle rank. Baigu had silver, copper, and iron. It had Mount Wutai. Fanshi was middle rank. Guo was middle rank. It had Shimen Pass. Tanglin, originally Wuyan, was a middle-ranked county created from Wutai and Guo and renamed in Tanglong 1. Yun Prefecture, Yunzhong Commandery, was a lower-ranked area command. In the fourteenth year of Zhenguan the seat was moved from North Dingxiang City in Shuozhou to Dingxiang County. In the first year of Yongchun it was overrun by Mojie; the population was moved to Shuozhou. It was restored in the eighteenth year of Kaiyuan. Its local tribute included yak tails and hawk feathers. It had 3,169 households and a population of 7,930. It administered one county. It had Pinglu Army, established at the beginning of Kaiyuan. To the east was Zhen'an Army, originally Yanjun Garrison City; in Zhenyuan year two it became an army city. Four hundred eighty li west was Yuguan Garrison City. It also had four garrison cities: Ruluo, Huaiyuan, Wulü, and Xiangping. It had two frontier garrisons: Yunzhong and Loufan. East of the city lay Niupi Pass. Yunzhong now includes its origin as Hengan Garrison, the North Heng Prefecture and Dingxiang County episodes, and the two military routes. Shuo Prefecture, Mayi Commandery, was lower-ranked. The seat was originally at Shanyang; in the Jianzhong era Military Commissioner Ma Sui moved it to Mayi, then later restored the former seat. Its local tribute included white hawk feathers, leopard tails, and licorice. It had 5,493 households and a population of 24,533. It administered two counties. Shanyang and Mayi now include their middle rank, the Changning merger, and Mayi creation at Datong Army city. Wei Prefecture, Xingtang Commandery, was lower-ranked. It was formerly Anbian Commandery. It lay in the territory of Lingqiu in Sui's Yanmen Commandery and Feihu in Shanggu Commandery. In early Tang the Turks were defeated. In the sixth year of Wude the prefecture was established along with Lingqiu and Feihu counties, with a provisional seat at Yangqu. In the seventh year the provisional seat was at Fanshi. In the eighth year the provisional seat was at the old Northern Hengzhou city in Xiurong. In the fifth year of Zhenguan the Turks were defeated, the former territory recovered, and the seat returned to Lingqiu. In early Kaiyuan the seat was moved to Anbian. In the second year of Zhide the commandery designation was changed and the former seat restored. Its local tribute included bear hides, leopard tails, and pine nuts. It had 5,052 households and a population of 20,958. It administered three counties. Lingqiu was middle rank. It had Zhigu Pass. To its north were Kongling Pass and Da'an Fort. Feihu and Xingtang now include their ranks, Feihu temporary seat and copper works, and Xingtang former name at Hengye Army. Wu Prefecture. The entry is deficient. It administered one county. Wende. Xin Prefecture. The entry is deficient. It administered four counties. Yongxing, Fanshan, Longmen, and Huai'an. Lu Prefecture, Shangdang Commandery designation, great-area military governorship. Its local tribute included coarse cloth, ginseng, rock honey, and ink. It had 68,391 households and a population of 388,661. It administered ten counties. It had Yiwu Army, established in Jianzhong year four. To the west was Beiping Army, established during Kaiyuan. Anxi was close-ranked. It was originally Xianyu; in Wude year four its name was changed. Yifeng was close-ranked. In Wansui Tongtian year two its name was changed to Lijie because of resistance to the Khitan, and in Shenlong year one its former name was restored. Beiping was upper-ranked. In Wansui Tongtian year two its name was changed to Xunzhong because of resistance to the Khitan, and in Shenlong year one its former name was restored. Northwest was the old Anyang Pass. Wangdu was upper-ranked. It was established in Wude year four. Quyang was upper-ranked. It was originally Hengyang; in Yuanhe year fifteen its name was changed, and that year Hengyue was also changed to Zhenyue, with a shrine to the Marchmount. Xingyi was middle-ranked. It was originally Suichang; in Wude year four it was called Tangchang, and in Tianbao year one its name was changed. Tang was upper-ranked. It had one garrison command: Kanli. Shangdang, Huguan, and Changzi now include their ranks, Xuanzong old residence, palace and mountain notes, and Huguan creation from Shangdang. Tunliu was upper rank. It had the Three Song Mountains. Lucheng was upper-ranked. In Tianyou year two it was changed to Luzi. Xiangyuan was upper-ranked. In Wude year one, Hanzhou was established from Xiangyuan, Licheng, She, Tongdi, and Xiang; in Zhenguan year seventeen the province was abolished, and all the counties came under this prefecture. To the east was the old Jinggu Pass. Licheng was upper-ranked. In Tianyou year two it was changed to Liting. It had Copper Mountain. To the east was the old Hukou Pass. She was middle-ranked. Lucheng, Xiangyuan, Licheng, and She were middle rank. It had iron deposits. Tongdi and Wuxiang now include their ranks, Jiashui County, prefectural transfers, Wuxiang former names, and Angche Pass. Ze Prefecture, Gaoping Commandery, was upper-ranked. It was formerly Changping Commandery, seated at Huoze; in the eighth year of Wude the seat moved to Duanshi; in the first year of Zhenguan to Jincheng; in the first year of Tianbao the commandery designation was changed. Its local tribute included ginseng, quartz, and pheasants. It had 27,822 households and a population of 157,090. It administered six counties. It had five garrison commands: Danchuan, Yonggu, Ping'an, Qinshui, and Baizhuang. Jincheng was upper-ranked. It was originally Danchuan. In Wude year one Jianzhou was established. In year three Jincheng was divided from Danchuan and established to belong to it. In year six the province was abolished and it belonged to Gaizhou, and Gaizhou was moved to govern there. In year nine Danchuan and Gaicheng were abolished into Jincheng. In Zhenguan year one the province was abolished, and Jincheng, Gaoping, and Lingchuan came under this prefecture. In Tianyou year two it was changed to Danchuan. To the south was Tianjing Pass, also called Taihang Pass. Duanshi was middle-ranked. Jincheng and Duanshi were middle rank. It had Mount Kui. Lingchuan was middle rank. Yangcheng and Qinshui now include their middle rank, Yangcheng former name, later reversion, and metal resources. Gaoping. It was upper-ranked. It was originally Sui's Changping Commandery. In Wude year one it was called Gaizhou, governing Gaoping, Danchuan, and Lingchuan counties, and Gaicheng County was also divided off and established to belong to it. It had Xuan River, also called Dan River; in Zhenyuan year one the magistrate Ming Ji led it into the city, and it was called Sweet Spring. It had the Valley for Redressing Wrongs, originally Killing Valley; when Xuanzong visited Luzhou and passed it, its name was changed. To the north was Changping Pass.

右河東採訪使，治蒲州。 河北道河北道，蓋古幽、冀二州之境，漢河內、魏、渤海、清河、平原、常山、上谷、涿、漁陽、右北平、遼西、真定、中山、信都、河間、廣陽等郡國，又參有東郡、河東、上黨、鉅鹿之地。 孟、懷、澶、衞及魏、博、相之南境為娵訾分，邢、洺、惠、貝、冀、深、趙、鎮、定及魏、博、相之北境為大梁分，滄、景、德為玄枵分，瀛、莫、幽、易、涿、平、媯、檀、薊、營、安東為析木津分。 為州二十九，都護府一，縣百七十四。 其名山：林慮、白鹿、封龍、井陘、碣石、常岳。 其大川：漳、淇、呼陀。 厥賦：絲、絹、綿。 厥貢：羅、綾、紬、紗、鳳翮葦席。 孟州孟州，望。 建中二年，以河南府之河陽、河清、濟源、溫租賦入河陽三城使，又以汜水租賦益之。 會昌三年遂以五縣為州。 土貢：黃魚䱹。 縣五。 河陽，汜水，河陰，溫，濟源。 懷州懷州河內郡，雄。 武德二年沒王世充，僑治濟源之柏崖城。 貴鄉，望。有西渠，開元二十八年，刺史盧暈徙永濟渠，自石灰窠引流至城西，注魏橋，以通江、淮之貨。元城，望。貞觀十七年省入貴鄉，聖曆二年復置。魏，望。武德四年置漳陰縣，貞觀元年省入焉。館陶，望。武德五年，以館陶、冠氏及博州之堂邑，貝州之臨清、清水置毛州，并析臨清置沙丘縣。貞觀元年州廢，省清水入冠氏，省沙丘入臨清，餘縣皆還故屬。冠氏，望。莘，上。武德五年以莘、臨黃、武陽、博州之武水置莘州，貞觀元年州廢，縣還故屬。朝城，緊。本武陽，貞觀十七年省入臨黃、莘。永昌元年復置，曰武聖。開元七年更名。元和中隸澶州，後復來屬。天祐三年更曰武陽，又以武陽、莘河外地入鄆州。昌樂，望。武德五年置，貞觀十八年省繁水入焉。臨河，上。武德二年隸黎州，貞觀十七年省澶水縣入焉。澶水，本澶淵，避高祖名更。州廢，隸相州，天祐三年來屬。洹水，上。本隸相州，天祐三年來屬。成安，上。本隸相州，天祐二年更名斥丘，三年來屬。內黃，緊。本隸相州，武德四年析置繁陽縣，隸黎州，貞觀元年省，天祐三年來屬。宗城，望。本隸貝州。武德四年，以宗城、經城及冀州之南山宮斌彊置宗州，析經城置府城縣。九年州廢，省府城入經城，省斌彊入清河，餘縣皆還故屬。天祐三年曰廣宗，是歲來屬。永濟。上。本隸貝州，大曆七年，田承嗣析魏州之臨清置。天祐三年來屬。博州博平郡，上。 上。武德二年以縣置黎州，尋沒竇建德。四年，建德平，復以黎陽、臨河、內黃、澶水，魏州觀城、頓丘，相州之蕩源置；是年，以頓丘、觀城還隸魏州，蕩源還隸相州。貞觀十七年州廢，省澶水，以黎陽來屬，內黃、臨河隸相州。有白馬津，一名黎陽關。有大岯山，一名黎陽山。有新河，元和八年，觀察使田弘正及鄭滑節度使薛平開，長十四里，闊六十步，深丈有七尺，決河注故道，滑州遂無水患。貝州清河郡，望。 貝州貝州清河郡，望。
