容城，上。本遒。武德五年，以容城及幽州之固安、歸義置北義州。貞觀元年州廢，縣還故屬。聖曆二年以拒契丹更名全忠，神龍二年復故名，天寶元年又更名。遂城，上。 淶水，上。 滿城，中。本永樂，天寶元年更名。有郎山。有永清軍，貞元十五年置。五回。中下。開元二十三年析易置，幷置樓亭、板城二縣。天寶後省。 幽州范陽郡，大都督府。 本涿郡，天寶元年更名。 土貢：綾、綿、絹、角弓、人葠、栗。 戶六萬七千二百四十三，口三十七萬一千三百一十二。 縣九。 有府十四，曰呂平、涿城、德聞、潞城、樂上、清化、洪源、良鄉、開福、政和、停驂、柘河、良杜、咸寧。 城內有經略軍，又有納降軍，本納降守捉城，故丁零川也。 西南有安塞軍，有赫連城。 有宗王、乾澗、殄寇三鎮城，召堆、車坊、蒿城、河旁四戍。 薊，望。天寶元年析置廣寧縣，三載省。有鐵。有故隋臨朔宮。幽都，望。本薊縣地。隋於營州之境汝羅故城置遼西郡，以處粟末靺鞨降人。武德元年曰燕州，領縣三：遼西、瀘河、懷遠。土貢：豹尾。是年，省瀘河。六年自營州遷于幽州城中，以首領世襲刺史。貞觀元年省懷遠。開元二十五年徙治幽州北桃谷山。天寶元年曰歸德郡。戶二千四十五，口萬一千六百三。建中二年為朱滔所滅，因廢為縣。廣平，上。天寶元年析薊置，三載省，至德後復置。潞，上。武德二年自無終徙漁陽郡於此，置玄州，領潞、漁陽，幷置臨泃縣。貞觀元年州廢，省臨泃、無終，以潞、漁陽來屬。武清，上。本雍奴，天寶元年更名。永清，緊。本武隆，如意元年析安次置，景雲元年曰會昌，天寶元年更名。安次，上。良鄉，望。聖曆元年曰固節，神龍元年復故名。有大防山。昌平。 薊，幽都，廣平，潞，武清，永清，安次，上。 良鄉，昌平。 望。 北十五里有軍都陘。 西北三十五里有納款關，即居庸故關，亦謂之軍都關。 其北有防禦軍，古夏陽川也。 有狼山。 涿州涿州，上。 大曆四年，節度使朱希彩表析幽州之范陽、歸義、固安置。 縣五。 范陽，望。本涿，武德七年更名。歸義，上。武德五年置，貞觀元年省，八年復置。景雲二年隸鄚州，是年，還隸幽州。固安，上。 新昌，上。大曆四年析固安置。新城。上。大和六年以故督亢地置。 瀛州河間郡，上。 土貢：絹。 戶九萬八千一十八，口六十六萬三千一百七十一。 縣五。 河間，高陽，平舒，上。 束城，上。 景城。 莫州文安郡，上。 本鄚州，景雲二年，以瀛州之鄚、任丘、文安、清苑、唐興，幽州之歸義置。 開元十三年以「鄚」「鄭」文相類，更名。 土貢：絹、綿。 戶五萬三千四百九十三，口三十三萬九千九百七十二。 縣六。 莫，清苑，上。 文安，任丘，長豐，唐興。 平州平州北平郡，下。 初治臨渝，武德元年徙治盧龍。 土貢：熊鞹、蔓荊實、人葠。 戶三千一百一十三，口二萬五千八十六。 縣三。 盧龍，石城，馬城。 媯州媯州媯川郡，上。 本北燕州，武德七年平高開道，以幽州之懷戎置。 貞觀八年更名。 土貢：樺皮、胡祿、甲榆、𩩉矢、麝香。 戶二千二百六十三，口萬一千五百八十四。 縣一。 有府二，曰密雲、白檀。 有清夷軍，垂拱中置。 有淮北、白陽度、雲治、廣邊四鎮兵。 有橫河、柴城二戍。 有陽門城。 有永定、窯子二關。 又有懷柔軍，在媯、蔚二州之境。 懷戎。 上。 天寶中析置媯川縣，尋省。 媯水貫中。 北九十里有長城，開元中張說築。 東南五十里有居庸塞，東連盧龍、碣石，西屬太行、常山，實天下之險。 有鐵門關。 西有寧武軍。 又北有廣邊軍，故白雲城也。 檀州檀州密雲郡，本安樂郡，天寶元年更名。 土貢：人葠、麝香。 戶六千六十四，口三萬二百四十六。 縣二。 密雲，中。 有隗山。 燕樂。 中。 東北百八十五里有東軍、北口二守捉。 北口，長城口也。 又北八百里有吐護真河，奚王衙帳也。 薊州薊州漁陽郡，下。 開元十八年析幽州置。 土貢：白膠。 戶五千三百一十七，口萬八千五百二十一。 縣三。 漁陽，三河，玉田。 營州營州柳城郡，上都督府。 本遼西郡，萬歲通天元年為契丹所陷，聖曆二年僑治漁陽，開元五年又還治柳城，天寶元年更名。 土貢：人葠、麝香、豹尾、皮骨𩨸。 戶九百九十七，口三千七百八十九。 縣一。 柳城。 中。 西北接奚，北接契丹，有東北鎮醫巫閭山祠。 又東有碣石山。 安東都護府安東，上都護府。 總章元年，李勣平高麗國，得城百七十六，分其地為都督府九，州四十二，縣一百，置安東都護府於平壤城以統之，用其酋渠為都督、刺史、縣令。 上元三年徙遼東郡故城，儀鳳二年又徙新城。 聖曆元年更名安東都督府，神龍元年復故名。 開元二年徙于平州，天寶二年|743年又徙于遼西故郡城。 至德後廢。 土貢：人葠。 有安東守捉。有懷遠軍，天寶二載743年置。又有保定軍。
At right: the Hedong Surveillance Commissioner, with his seat at Puzhou. The Hebei Circuit lay within ancient You and Ji, covering the Han commanderies and principalities of Henei, Wei, Bohai, Qinghe, Pingyuan, Changshan, Shanggu, Zhuo, Yuyang, Right Beiping, Liaoxi, Zhending, Zhongshan, Xindu, Hejian, and Guangyang, with portions of Dong, Hedong, Shangdang, and Julu as well. Meng, Huai, Chan, Wei, and the southern portions of Wei, Bo, and Xiang fell within the Zuzi asterism division; Xing, Ming, Hui, Bei, Ji, Shen, Zhao, Zhen, Ding, and the northern portions of Wei, Bo, and Xiang within the Daliang division; Cang, Jing, and De within the Xuanxiao division; and Ying, Mo, You, Yi, Zhuo, Ping, Gui, Tan, Ji, Ying, and Andong within the Ximu Ford division. It comprised twenty-nine prefectures, one protectorate, and one hundred seventy-four counties. Its notable mountains were Linlu, Bailu, Fenglong, Jingxing, Jieshi, and Changyue. Its major rivers were the Zhang, Qi, and Hutuo. Its assessed tribute consisted of silk, gauze, and cotton. Its presented tribute included gauze, damask, pongee, yarn, and phoenix-wing reed mats. Meng Prefecture, distinguished rank. In the second year of Jianzhong the tax revenues of Heyang, Heqing, Jiyuan, and Wen from Henan Superior Prefecture were assigned to the Heyang Three Cities Commissioner, augmented by the revenues of Sishui. In the third year of Huichang the five counties were constituted as a prefecture. Its local tribute included yellow croaker. It administered five counties. Heyang, Sishui, Heyin, Wen, and Jiyuan. Huai Prefecture, Henei Commandery designation, powerful rank. In the second year of Wude it fell to Wang Shichong and the seat was provisionally at Baiya City in Jiyuan. In the fourth year, with Shichong subdued, the former seat was restored. Its local tribute included plain gauze, plain pongee, bitter orange peel, tea, and ox-knee herb. It had 55,349 households and a population of 318,126. It administered five counties. It had two garrison commands: Danshui and Wuze. Henei was eminent. In Wude year three, Taihang, Zhongyi, and Ziling counties were divided off and established, and Gudan County was divided from Heyang and established. In year four they were all abolished. It had Taihang Mountain. It had Dan River, renamed Huai River in Kaiyuan year eleven. Wude was eminent. It was originally Anchang; in Wude year two its name was changed, and that year Northern Yizhou was established. In year four the province was abolished and it came under this prefecture. One hundred li north was the old Dahu Pass on Taihang Mountain. Huojia was eminent. In Wude year four, Yinzhou was established from Huojia, Wuzhi, Xiuwu, Xinxiang, and Gongcheng, and Bowang County was also established. In Zhenguan year one the province was abolished; Huojia, Wuzhi, and Xiuwu came under this prefecture, while Xinxiang, Gongcheng, and Bowang belonged to Weizhou. Wuzhi was eminent. In Zhenguan year one Huai County was abolished into it. Xiuwu was close-ranked. In Wude year two, Li Houde, a commoner of Henei, surrendered with Zhuolu City; Zhizhou was established, and Xiuwu County was also established. In year four the county seat was moved to old Xiuwu, Xiuwu was changed to Wuzhi, and a separate Xiuwu County was established. That year the province was abolished and it belonged to Yinzhou. Twenty li northwest was New River, which combined with Huangdan Spring water below Liuzhen Mountain and flowed south into Wuze Marsh; the magistrate Du opened it. Weizhou, Wei Commandery, was a grand commandery governor's office and was strong. Henei, Wude, Huojia, Wuzhi, and Xiuwu. Wei Prefecture, Wei Commandery designation, great-area military governorship, powerful rank. It was formerly Wuyang Commandery; renamed Ji Prefecture in the second year of Longshuo, restored as Wei Prefecture in the third year of Xianheng, and the commandery designation changed in the first year of Tianbao. Its local tribute included patterned pongee, cotton pongee, plain pongee, silk tabby, silk, and purple madder. It had 151,596 households and a population of 1,109,873. It administered fourteen counties. Guixiang was eminent. It had Western Canal; in Kaiyuan year twenty-eight the prefect Lu Yun shifted Yongji Canal, drawing its flow from Shihuike to the west of the city and pouring it into Wei Bridge, in order to convey goods from the Yangzi and Huai regions. Yuancheng was eminent. In Zhenguan year seventeen it was abolished into Guixiang, and in Shengli year two it was restored. Wei was eminent. In Wude year four Zhangyin County was established, and in Zhenguan year one it was abolished into Wei. Guantao was eminent. In Wude year five, Maozhou was established from Guantao, Guanshi, Tangyi of Bozhou, and Linqing and Qingshui of Beizhou, and Shaqiu County was divided from Linqing and established. In Zhenguan year one the province was abolished; Qingshui was abolished into Guanshi, Shaqiu was abolished into Linqing, and the remaining counties all returned to their former jurisdictions. Guanshi was eminent. Shen was upper-ranked. In Wude year five, Shenzhou was established from Shen, Linhuang, Wuyang, and Wushui of Bozhou; in Zhenguan year one the province was abolished and the counties returned to their former jurisdictions. Chaocheng was close-ranked. It was originally Wuyang; in Zhenguan year seventeen it was abolished into Linhuang and Shen. In Yongchang year one it was restored and called Wusheng. In Kaiyuan year seven its name was changed. During Yuanhe it belonged to Chanzhou, and later again came under this prefecture. In Tianyou year three it was changed to Wuyang, and the territory of Wuyang and Shen beyond the Yellow River was also put into Yunzhou. Changle was eminent. It was established in Wude year five, and in Zhenguan year eighteen Fanshui was abolished into it. Linhe was upper-ranked. In Wude year two it belonged to Lizhou, and in Zhenguan year seventeen Chanshui County was abolished into it. Chanshui was originally Chanyuan; its name was changed to avoid Gaozu's personal name. When the province was abolished, it belonged to Xiangzhou, and in Tianyou year three it came under this prefecture. Huanshui was upper-ranked. It originally belonged to Xiangzhou and in Tianyou year three came under this prefecture. Cheng'an was upper-ranked. It originally belonged to Xiangzhou; in Tianyou year two its name was changed to Chiqiu, and in year three it came under this prefecture. Neihuang was close-ranked. It originally belonged to Xiangzhou; in Wude year four Fanyang County was divided off and established and belonged to Lizhou; in Zhenguan year one it was abolished, and in Tianyou year three it came under this prefecture. Zongcheng was eminent. It originally belonged to Beizhou. In Wude year four, Zongzhou was established from Zongcheng, Jingcheng, and Nanxiangong and Binjiang of Jizhou, and Fucheng County was divided from Jingcheng and established. In year nine the province was abolished; Fucheng was abolished into Jingcheng, Binjiang was abolished into Qinghe, and the remaining counties all returned to their former jurisdictions. In Tianyou year three it was called Guangzong, and that year it came under this prefecture. Yongji was upper-ranked. It originally belonged to Beizhou. In Dali year seven, Tian Chengsi divided Linqing of Weizhou to establish it. In Tianyou year three it came under this prefecture. Bozhou, Boping Commandery, was upper-ranked. Guixiang, Yuancheng, Wei, Guantao, and Guanshi were distinguished rank. Shen, Chaocheng, Changle, Linhe, Huanshui, Cheng'an, Neihuang, and Yongji. Bo Prefecture, Boping Commandery designation, upper rank. In the fourth year of Wude it was established from Liaocheng, Wushui, Tangyi, and Gaotang of Wei Prefecture. Its local tribute included damask and plain pongee. It had 52,631 households and a population of 408,252. It administered six counties. Liaocheng, Boping, and Wushui were upper rank. Qingping and Tangyi were upper rank. Gaotang was upper-ranked; it was briefly renamed Chongwu and then restored to its old name. Xiang Prefecture, Ye Commandery, was eminent. It was formerly Wei Commandery and was renamed in the first year of Tianbao. Its local tribute included yarn, silk, barrier cloth, phoenix-wing mats, flower-mouth gourds, anemarrhena root, and lead powder. It had 101,142 households and a population of 591,196. It administered six counties. Anyang, Ye, Tangyin, and Linlu were upper rank. Yaocheng and Linzhang. Wei Prefecture, Ji Commandery designation, distinguished rank. The seat was originally at Wei; in the first year of Zhenguan it was moved to Ji. Its local tribute included damask, silk, cotton, and lead powder. It had 48,056 households and a population of 284,630. It administered five counties. Ji, Wei, Gongcheng, and Xinxiang were distinguished rank. To its northeast lay the former Linqing Pass. To its southeast lay the former Yanjin Pass. Liyang. It was upper-ranked. In Wude year two Lizhou was established from the county, but soon fell to Dou Jiande. In year four, after Jiande was pacified, it was again established from Liyang, Linhe, Neihuang, Chanshui, Guancheng and Dunqiu of Weizhou, and Dangyuan of Xiangzhou. That year Dunqiu and Guancheng were returned to Weizhou, and Dangyuan was returned to Xiangzhou. In Zhenguan year seventeen the province was abolished; Chanshui was abolished, Liyang came under this prefecture, and Neihuang and Linhe belonged to Xiangzhou. It had Baima Ford, also called Liyang Pass. It had Dapi Mountain, also called Liyang Mountain. It had New River; in Yuanhe year eight the surveillance commissioner Tian Hongzheng and Xue Ping, military governor of Zheng-Hua, opened it. It was fourteen li long, sixty paces wide, and one zhang seven chi deep; it breached the Yellow River and poured into its old channel, so Huazhou no longer suffered flood damage. Beizhou, Qinghe Commandery, was eminent. Bei Prefecture, Qinghe Commandery designation, distinguished rank. The seat was originally at Qinghe; in the sixth year of Wude it was moved to Liting; in the eighth year the former seat was restored. Its local tribute included silk, felt, and saddle-cover felt. It had 100,015 households and a population of 834,757. It administered eight counties. Qinghe was close-administered rank. Qingyang and Wucheng now include Qingyang close rank, the brief Xiajin County, and Wucheng upper rank. Jingcheng, Linqing, and Zhangnan now include their ranks, Zhangjia River, and Linqing transfer history. Liting was upper rank. Xiajin was upper-ranked, originally Shu, and renamed in Tianbao 1. Chan Prefecture was upper-ranked. In the fourth year of Wude it was established from Chanshui in Li Prefecture and Dunqiu and Guancheng in Wei Prefecture. In the first year of Zhenguan the prefecture was abolished and the counties returned to their former jurisdictions. In the seventh year of Dali, Tian Chengsi petitioned to restore it with Dunqiu and Linhuang from Wei Prefecture. Its local tribute included horn bows, phoenix-wing mats, and lead powder. It administered four counties. Dunqiu was distinguished rank. Qingfeng, Guancheng, and Linhuang now include Qingfeng naming, Guancheng rank, and Guancheng abolition and restoration. Close-administered rank. To its southeast was Lujin Pass, also called Gaoling Ford. Xing Prefecture, Julu Commandery designation, upper rank. It was formerly Xiangguo Commandery and was renamed in the first year of Tianbao. Its local tribute included silk cloth, porcelain, knives, and ornamental stone. It had 70,189 households and a population of 382,798. It administered eight counties. Longgang, Shahe, Nanhe, Julu, Pingxiang, Ren, Yaoshan, and Neiqiu. Ming Prefecture, Guangping Commandery designation, distinguished rank. It was formerly Wu'an Commandery and was renamed in the first year of Tianbao. Its local tribute included silk tabby, cotton, pongee, and oiled garments. It had 91,666 households and a population of 683,280. It administered six counties. Yongnian was distinguished rank. Ping'en was upper rank. Linming was close-ranked. In Wude year one, Zizhou was established from Linming, Wu'an, Feixiang, and Handan; in year four the province was abolished and all the counties belonged to Cizhou; in year six Linming and Feixiang came under this prefecture. On Gou Mountain were Taizong's old ramparts; he campaigned against Liu Heita there. Jize was upper-ranked. It was established in Wude year four. It had Pule County, established at the beginning of Wude; later it fell to Dou Jiande and was then abolished. It had two southern dikes on the Zhang and Ming rivers and one southern dike on the Sha River, built in Yonghui year five. Feixiang was upper-ranked. The province also governed Qingzhang and Chishui counties. In Huichang year three Qingzhang was abolished into Feixiang and Chishui into Quzhou. Quzhou was upper-ranked. It was established in Wude year four. Huizhou was upper-ranked. It was originally Cizhou; in Wude year one it was established from Fuyang, Linshui, and Cheng'an of Xiangzhou. Linming, Jize, Feixiang, and Quzhou. Hui Prefecture, upper rank; originally Ci Prefecture; in the first year of Wude it was established from Fuyang, Linshui, and Cheng'an of Xiang Prefecture. In the first year of Zhenguan the prefecture was abolished and Fuyang and Cheng'an returned to Xiang Prefecture. In the first year of Yongtai, Zhaoyi Military Commissioner Xue Song petitioned to restore it with Fuyang from Xiang Prefecture and Handan and Wu'an from Ming Prefecture. In the third year of Tianyou it was renamed because the characters for 'ci' and 'hui' sounded alike. Its local tribute included yarn and magnetite. It administered four counties. Fuyang was distinguished rank. Handan, Wuan, and Zhaoyi now include their ranks, transfers, former name, restoration, and metal notes. Zhen Prefecture, Changshan Commandery, was a great area command. It was formerly Heng Prefecture, Hengshan Commandery, seated at Shiyi; established in the first year of Yining from Sui's Gaoyang Commandery. In the fourth year of Wude the seat was moved to Zhending. In the first year of Tianbao the commandery designation was changed; in the fifteenth year it was called Pingshan, soon restored as Hengshan. In the fifteenth year of Yuanhe it was renamed to avoid the taboo name of Emperor Muzong. Its local tribute included peacock gauze, melon-seed gauze, spring gauze, and pears. It had 54,633 households and a population of 342,134. It administered eleven counties. It had the Hengyang Army, established in the Kaiyuan era. Zhending was eminent. In Wude year six Hengshan County was divided off and established, and in Zhenguan year one it was abolished. In Zaichu year one it was called Zhongshan, and in Shenlong year one its former name was restored. Gaocheng was close-ranked. In Yining year one Julu Commandery was established, and Baisi, Xinfeng, and Yi'an counties were also divided off and established. In Wude year one it was called Lianzhou. In year four, Gucheng of Zhaozhou, Wuji of Dingzhou, and Lucheng of Jizhou were assigned to it, and Baisi, Xinfeng, and Yi'an were abolished into Gaocheng. In Zhenguan year one the province was abolished; Lucheng belonged to Shenzhou, Gucheng and Wuji belonged to Dingzhou, and Gaocheng came under this prefecture. In Tianyou year two it was changed to Gaoping. Shiyi was close-ranked. Jiumen was upper-ranked. In Yining year one Jiumen Commandery was established, and Xinshi and Xinyi counties were also divided off and established. In Wude year one it was called Guanzhou; in year five the province was abolished, Xinyi and Xinshi were abolished, and Jiumen came under this prefecture. Xingtang was middle-ranked. In Wude year four Yucheng County was established, and in year five Ziyang County was abolished into it. In Changshou year two it was called Zhangwu, and in Shenlong year one its former name was restored. In Dali year three Dizhou was established from the county, and Lingshou and Hengyang of Dingzhou were also assigned to it. In year nine the province was abolished and the counties returned to their former jurisdictions. Jingxing was middle-ranked. In Yining year one Jingxing Commandery was established, and Weize County was also divided off and established. In Wude year one it was called Jingzhou, and later it also governed Luquan, Fangshan, Puwu, and Lingshou. In Zhenguan year one Puwu was abolished into Fangshan, and Luquan and Weize into Jingxing. In year seventeen the province was abolished, and all the counties came under this prefecture. It had iron. It had Lige Mountain. Pingshan was middle-ranked. It was originally Fangshan. In Yining year one Fangshan Commandery was established, and Puwu County was also established. In Wude year one it was called Yuezhou; in year four the province was abolished and all the counties belonged to Jingzhou. In Tianbao year fifteen its name was changed. It had iron. It had Baima Pass. It had Fang Mountain. Huolu was middle-ranked. It was originally Luquan; in Tianbao year fifteen its name was changed. It had the old Jingxing Pass, also called Tumen Pass. Ten li northeast was Datang Canal, which ran from Pingshan to Shiyi and drew Taibai Canal to irrigate fields. It had Lijiao Canal; in Zongzhang year two it drew Taibai Canal from northwest of Shiyi eastward into the territory of Zhending to irrigate fields. In Tianbao year two, 743, Datang Canal was again drawn from Shiyi southeast for forty-three li into Taibai Canal. It had Baodu Mountain. Lingshou was middle-ranked. In Yining year one Yanzhou was established from the county; in year four the province was abolished and it belonged to Jingzhou. Gucheng was middle-ranked. It originally belonged to Dingzhou, and in Dali year three it came under this prefecture. Luancheng was middle-ranked. It originally belonged to Zhaozhou; in Dali year two it came under this prefecture, and in Tianyou year two its name was changed to Luanshi. Jizhou, Xindu Commandery, was upper-ranked. Zhending, Gaocheng, and Shiyi were close-administered rank. Jiumen, Xingtang, Jingxing, Pingshan, Huolu, Lingshou, Gucheng, and Luancheng. Ji Prefecture, Xindu Commandery designation, upper rank. The seat was originally at Xindu; in the sixth year of Wude moved to Xiabo; in the first year of Zhenguan restored to the former seat; renamed Wei Prefecture in the second year of Longshuo; restored to the former name in the third year of Xianheng. Its local tribute included silk and cotton. It had 113,885 households and a population of 830,520. It administered nine counties. Xindu was eminent. In Tianyou year two it was changed to Yaodu. Two li east was Gerong Embankment; in Zhenguan year eleven the prefect Li Xinggong opened it, drawing Zhaozhao Canal water to pour into it. Nangong was eminent. Fifty-nine li west was the Zhuozhang Dike, built in Xianqing year one. It had Tongli Canal, opened in Yanzai year one. Tangyang was upper-ranked. Thirty li southwest was a canal that entered the county territory from Julu and flowed down into Nangong, opened in Jinglong year one. Ten li west was the Zhang River Dike, built in Kaiyuan year six. Zaoqiang was upper-ranked. Wuyi was upper-ranked. In Wude year four Changting County was divided off and established; in Zhenguan year one it was abolished. Thirty li north was the right dike of the Hengzhang, built in Xianqing year one. Hengshui was upper-ranked. Xindu, Nangong, Tangyang, and Zaoqiang were upper rank. Wuyi and Hengshui were upper rank. One li to the south lay the Magistrate Yang Canal; in the early Zai era Magistrate Yang Yuangui diverted the Zhang River northward, channeling it through the city to fill the moat. Fucheng, Tiao, and Wuqiang now include ranks, Fucheng later name, and Wuqiang repeated transfers. Shen Prefecture, Raoyang Commandery, was upper-ranked. In the fourth year of Wude it was established from Anping in Ding Prefecture and Raoyang in Ying Prefecture; the seat was soon moved to Raoyang. In the seventeenth year of Zhenguan the prefecture was abolished and the counties returned to their former jurisdictions. In the second year of Xiantian it was restored with Raoyang from Ying Prefecture, Lucheng, Xiabo, and Wuqiang from Ji Prefecture, and Anping from Ding Prefecture. Its local tribute included silk. It had 18,825 households and a population of 346,472. It administered seven counties. Luze, Raoyang, Shulu, and Anping were upper rank. Anling was eminent and briefly transferred to Jing Prefecture in Jingfu 1 before returning. Zhao Prefecture, Zhao Commandery designation, distinguished rank. In early Wude the seat was at Baixiang; in the fourth year moved to Pingji; in the fifth year renamed Luan Prefecture; in early Zhenguan restored to the former name. Its local tribute included silk. It had 63,454 households and a population of 395,238. It administered eight counties. Pingji, Ningjin, Zhaoqing, and Baixiang were upper rank. To its west were the Thousand-Gold Canal and Ten-Thousand-Gold Weir, dredged and built in the Kaiyuan era by Magistrate Wang Zuo to drain accumulated floodwater. Gaoyi was middle rank. Lincheng and Zanhuang now include their middle rank and Lincheng former and later name. Yuanshi. Upper rank. It had Mount Ling and Mount Fenglong. Cang Prefecture, Jingcheng Commandery designation, upper rank. It was formerly Bohai Commandery, seated at Qingchi; in the first year of Wude moved to Rao'an; in the sixth year to Husu; in the first year of Zhenguan restored to Qingchi. Its local tribute included silk cloth, willow boxes, reed mats, sugar crabs, and snakehead fish. It had 124,024 households and a population of 825,705. It administered seven counties. Yanshan, Changlu, Leling, Rao'an, Wudi, and Qianfu. Jing Prefecture, upper rank. Rongcheng and Suicheng now include Rongcheng former name, North Yi Prefecture, resistance to the Khitan, and later renamings. In the first year of Changqing the prefecture was abolished and the counties returned to Cang Prefecture; in the second year it was restored with Gonggao, Dongguang, Linjin, Nanpi, and Jingcheng. In the fourth year of Dahe the prefecture was again abolished and the counties returned to Cang Prefecture. It was restored in the first year of Jingfu. Its local tribute included reed mats. It administered four counties. Gonggao and Dongguang were upper rank. Twenty li to the south lay the Jin River, opened in the Kaiyuan era to run from Anling into the Fu River. Linjin and Nanpi now include ranks, Linjin former name, the old Mao River, and Tangchang Army. De Prefecture, Pingyuan Commandery, was upper-ranked. Its local tribute included silk and damask. It had 83,211 households and a population of 659,855. It administered six counties. Ande was close-administered rank. Changhe was upper rank. To its southeast lay the former Zhanggong Pass. Pingyuan and Pingchang were both upper-ranked and were briefly assigned to Qi Prefecture before returning; Pingchang absorbed Ban County and had Majia River, known as "New River." Jiangling was eminent. Anling. Ding Prefecture, Boling Commandery designation, upper rank. It was formerly Gaoyang Commandery and was renamed in the first year of Tianbao. Its local tribute included gauze, pongee, fine damask, auspicious damask, paired-medallion damask, single-medallion damask, double-wrapped damask, and boiled-thread damask. It had 78,090 households and a population of 496,676. It administered ten counties. Anxi, Yifeng, Beiping, Wangdu, Quyang, Xingyi, and Tang were upper rank. It had copper and iron. To its northwest lay the former Badu Pass and Daoma Pass. To its north lay the former Weisu Pass. Xinle was middle rank. Twenty li to the southeast lay Mudao Ditch, named for a man named Mudao who lived beside it. Wuji was upper-ranked; its written "wu" was altered in Wansui Tongtian 2, and it had Mount Wuji. In Jingfu 2 Wang Chucun petitioned to make Qi Prefecture from Wuji and Shenze. Middle rank. Jingcheng now includes its upper rank and repeated transfers among Cang, Jing, and this prefecture. Its local tribute included pongee, cotton, and ink. It had 44,230 households and a population of 258,779. It administered six counties. It had nine garrison commands: Suicheng, Anyi, Xiuwu, Dexing, Xin'an, Guting, Wusui, Changle, and Longshui. It had the Gaoyang Army. Yi was upper rank. Rongcheng and Suicheng now include Rongcheng former name, North Yi Prefecture, resistance to the Khitan, and later renamings. Laishui was upper rank. Mancheng and Wuhui now include their ranks, Mancheng former name, Mount Lang, Yongqing Army, and the short-lived Wuhui county group. You Prefecture, Fanyang Commandery, was a great area command. It was formerly Zhuo Commandery and was renamed in the first year of Tianbao. Its local tribute included damask, cotton, silk, horn bows, ginseng, and chestnuts. It had 67,243 households and a population of 371,312. It administered nine counties. It had fourteen garrison commands: Lüping, Zhuocheng, Dewen, Lucheng, Leshang, Qinghua, Hongyuan, Liangxiang, Kaifu, Zhenghe, Ting'an, Zhehe, Liangdu, and Xianning. Within the city stood the Jinglue Army; there was also the Surrender Reception Army, originally the Surrender Reception garrison city in the old Dingling River region. To its southwest lay the Ansei Army and Helian City. It had three garrison cities—Zongwang, Qianjian, and Tiankou—and four outposts: Zhaodui, Chefang, Haocheng, and Hepang. Ji was eminent. In Tianbao year one Guangning County was divided off and established; in year three it was abolished. It had iron. It had the old Sui Linshuo Palace. Youdu was eminent. It was originally territory of Ji County. Sui established Liaoxi Commandery at old Ruluo City within the territory of Yingzhou to settle surrendered Sumo Mohe people. In Wude year one it was called Yanzhou and governed three counties: Liaoxi, Luhe, and Huaiyuan. Its tribute was leopard tails. That year Luhe was abolished. In year six it was moved from Yingzhou into the city of Youzhou, with its chieftains serving as hereditary prefects. In Zhenguan year one Huaiyuan was abolished. In Kaiyuan year twenty-five its seat was moved to Taogu Mountain north of Youzhou. In Tianbao year one it was called Guide Commandery. It had 2,045 households and 11,603 mouths. In Jianzhong year two it was destroyed by Zhu Tao, and was consequently abolished into a county. Guangping was upper-ranked. In Tianbao year one it was divided from Ji and established; in year three it was abolished, and after Zhide it was restored. Lu was upper-ranked. In Wude year two Yuyang Commandery was moved here from Wuzhong and Xuanzhou was established, governing Lu and Yuyang, and Linju County was also established. In Zhenguan year one the province was abolished; Linju and Wuzhong were abolished, and Lu and Yuyang came under this prefecture. Wuqing was upper-ranked. It was originally Yongnu; in Tianbao year one its name was changed. Yongqing was close-ranked. It was originally Wulong; in Ruyi year one it was divided from Anci and established; in Jingyun year one it was called Huichang, and in Tianbao year one its name was changed. Anci was upper-ranked. Liangxiang was eminent. In Shengli year one it was called Gujie, and in Shenlong year one its former name was restored. It had Dafang Mountain. Changping. Ji, Youdu, Guangping, Lu, Wuqing, Yongqing, and Anci were upper rank. Liangxiang and Changping. Distinguished rank. Fifteen li to the north lay Jundu Pass. Thirty-five li to the northwest lay Nakuan Pass, the former Juyong Pass, also called Jundu Pass. To its north lay the Defense Army in the ancient Xiayang River region. It had Langshan. Zhuo Prefecture, upper rank. In the fourth year of Dali, Military Commissioner Zhu Xicai petitioned to carve out Fanyang, Guiyi, and Gu'an from You Prefecture. It administered five counties. Fanyang, Guiyi, and Gu’an now include their ranks, Fanyang former name, and Guiyi abolition, restoration, and transfer history. Xinchang and Xincheng now include their upper rank and creation histories. Ying Prefecture, Hejian Commandery, was upper-ranked. Its local tribute included silk. It had 98,018 households and a population of 663,171. It administered five counties. Hejian, Gaoyang, and Pingshu were upper rank. Shucheng was upper rank. Jingcheng. Mo Prefecture, Wen’an Commandery, was upper-ranked. It was formerly Mao Prefecture; in the second year of Jingyun it was established from Mao, Renqiu, Wen'an, Qingyuan, and Tangxing in Ying Prefecture and Guiyi in You Prefecture. In the thirteenth year of Kaiyuan it was renamed because the characters for 'Mao' and 'Zheng' were graphically similar. Its local tribute included silk and cotton. It had 53,493 households and a population of 339,972. It administered six counties. Mo and Qingyuan were upper rank. Wen'an, Renqiu, Changfeng, and Tangxing. Ping Prefecture, Beiping Commandery designation, lower rank. The seat was originally at Linru; in the first year of Wude it was moved to Lulong. Its local tribute included bear hides, chaste-tree fruit, and ginseng. It had 3,113 households and a population of 25,086. It administered three counties. Lulong, Shicheng, and Macheng. Gui Prefecture, Guichuan Commandery designation, upper rank. It was formerly North Yan Prefecture; in the seventh year of Wude, with Gao Kaidao subdued, it was established from Huairou in You Prefecture. It was renamed in the eighth year of Zhenguan. Its local tribute included birch bark, Hu-lu wood, armor elm, arrow shafts, and musk. It had 2,263 households and a population of 11,584. It administered one county. It had two garrison commands: Miyun and Baitan. It had the Qingyi Army, established in the Chuigong era. It had four garrison forces: Huaibei, Baiyangdu, Yunzhi, and Guangbian. It had two outposts: Henghe and Chaicheng. It had Yangmen City. It had two passes: Yongding and Yaozi. There was also the Huairou Army, in the territory of Gui and Wei prefectures. Huairou. Upper rank. In the Tianbao era Guichuan County was carved out and soon abolished. The Gui River ran through its center. Ninety li to the north lay the Great Wall, built by Zhang Yue in the Kaiyuan era. Fifty li to the southeast lay Juyong Pass; eastward it connected with Lulong and Jieshi, westward with the Taihang and Changshan ranges—truly the greatest strategic barrier under Heaven. It had Tiemen Pass. To its west lay the Ningwu Army. Farther north lay the Guangbian Army at the old Baiyun City. Tan Prefecture, Miyun Commandery designation; formerly Anle Commandery; renamed in the first year of Tianbao. Its local tribute included ginseng and musk. It had 6,064 households and a population of 30,246. It administered two counties. Miyun was middle rank. It had Mount Kui. Yanle. Middle rank. One hundred eighty-five li to the northeast lay the Dongjun and Beikou frontier garrisons. Beikou was the Great Wall Pass. Eight hundred li farther north lay the Tuhuzhen River, the seat of the Xi king. Ji Prefecture, Yuyang Commandery designation, lower rank. It was established in the eighteenth year of Kaiyuan from You Prefecture. Its local tribute included white glue. It had 5,317 households and a population of 18,521. It administered three counties. Yuyang, Sanhe, and Yutian. Ying Prefecture, Liucheng Commandery designation, upper military governorship. It was formerly Liaoxi Commandery; in the first year of Wansui Tongtian it fell to the Khitan; in the second year of Shengli the seat was provisionally at Yuyang; in the fifth year of Kaiyuan it returned to Liucheng; renamed in the first year of Tianbao. Its local tribute included ginseng, musk, leopard tails, and hide-and-bone saddles. It had 997 households and a population of 3,789. It administered one county. Liucheng. Middle rank. To the northwest it bordered the Xi; to the north the Khitan; it had the Northeast Garrison Shrine to Mount Yiwulü. Farther east lay Mount Jieshi. The Andong Protectorate, upper protectorate. In the first year of Zongzhang, Li Ji subdued Goguryeo, taking one hundred seventy-six cities; the territory was divided into nine area commands, forty-two prefectures, and one hundred counties; the Andong Protectorate was established at Pyongyang to govern them, appointing their tribal chiefs as area commanders, prefects, and magistrates. In the third year of Shangyuan it was moved to the old Liaodong Commandery city; in the second year of Yifeng it was moved again to Xincheng. In the first year of Shengli it was renamed the Andong Area Command; in the first year of Shenlong it was restored to the former name. In the second year of Kaiyuan it was moved to Ping Prefecture; in the second year of Tianbao (743) it was moved again to the old Liaoxi commandery city. It was abolished after the Zhide era. Its local tribute included ginseng. It had Andong Garrison. It had Huaiyuan Army, established in Tianbao year two, 743. It also had Baoding Army.

右河北採訪使，治魏州。
